jobs.description:
Doctoral position in experimental characterization of semiconductor nanocrystals

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Optical Materials Engineering Laboratory (Prof. David J. Norris) in the Department of Mechanical and Process Engineering (D-MAVT) at ETH Zurich investigates the synthesis, growth, structure, and optical properties of nanomaterials. Our interdisciplinary and international team combines materials chemistry, optical spectroscopy, electron microscopy, theoretical modeling, and numerical simulation to understand and control materials at the nanoscale.

Project background

Nanometer-scale semiconductor crystallites exhibit optical properties (e.g., absorption and emission spectra) that are strongly dependent on their size. Because this property is useful for creating tunable optical materials for optoelectronic applications ranging from displays and infrared cameras to nanophotonics and quantum technologies, chemical syntheses have been developed that produce nanocrystals from various semiconductors. The most advanced protocols are those that lead to quasi-spherical particles (known as colloidal quantum dots). However, even state-of-the-art nanocrystal samples contain distributions in particle size and morphology that limit their optical performance.

Two classes of semiconductor nanocrystals have been discovered as exceptions to this rule. They display an unusual form of "discrete" growth, jumping between a series of specific sizes. In particular, "magic-sized" nanocrystals grow through a sequence of well-defined sizes. This observation suggests that nanocrystals with exceptionally precise dimensions may be possible.

The central aim of this project is to determine how closely individual magic-sized nanocrystals approach atomic-scale perfection and how their size, shape, composition, surface chemistry, and structure influence their optical properties. Advanced single-particle microscopy and spectroscopy will be used to uncover variations that are hidden in conventional measurements. The resulting understanding will guide the synthesis and optimization of semiconductor nanocrystals for applications requiring highly uniform optical properties.

Job description

The doctoral student will characterize semiconductor nanocrystals using complementary optical and structural experimental techniques. The initial focus will be on CdSe magic-sized nanocrystals, with the work subsequently expanding to nanocrystals of different sizes, compositions, surface treatments, and heterostructures, including core/shell and InP nanocrystals.

The project will investigate how variations in nanocrystal size, shape, composition, surface chemistry, and structure influence optical properties. Ensemble and single-particle spectroscopy will be used to quantify optical heterogeneity and determine how closely magic-sized nanocrystals approach atomic-scale perfection. Measurements will examine properties such as emission linewidths, excited-state dynamics, spectral fluctuations, and the suitability of selected nanocrystals as single-photon emitters.

These optical studies will be complemented by advanced structural characterization. In particular, the student will use cryogenic electron microscopy and single-particle analysis to determine the three-dimensional structures of semiconductor nanocrystals with near-atomic or atomic-scale resolution. The experiments will examine nanocrystal shape, including the possible truncation of tetrahedral magic-sized nanocrystals, and how it varies with particle size, material composition, surface treatment, and isolation procedure.

The doctoral student will work closely with researchers responsible for nanocrystal synthesis and theoretical modeling. This interaction is central to the project: advanced samples will be supplied for optical and structural measurements, while the characterization results will guide improvements in nanocrystal synthesis, surface treatment, and structural control. descriptionByLocale.it:
Posizione dottorale nella caratterizzazione sperimentale dei nanocristalli semiconduttori

100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato

stampa
Druppo

Il Laboratorio di Ingegneria dei Materiali Opticali (Prof. David J. Norris) nel Dipartimento di Ingegneria Meccanica e dei Processi (D-MAVT) presso ETH Zurich indaga la sintesi, la crescita, la struttura e le proprietà ottiche dei nanomateriali. Il nostro team interdisciplinare e internazionale combina chimica dei materiali, spettroscopia ottica, microscopia elettronica, modellazione teorica e simulazione numerica per comprendere e controllare i materiali alla nanoscala.

Sfondo del progetto

I cristalli semiconduttori su scala nanometrica presentano proprietà ottiche (ad esempio, spettro di assorbimento e di emissione) fortemente dipendenti dalle loro dimensioni. Poiché questa proprietà è utile per la creazione di materiali ottici sintonizzabili per applicazioni optoelettroniche che vanno da display e telecamere a infrarossi a nanofotonici e tecnologie quantiche, sintesi chimiche sono state sviluppate che producono nanocristalli da vari semiconduttori. I protocolli più avanzati sono quelli che portano a particelle quasi-sferiche (conosciute come punti quantici colloidali). Tuttavia, anche campioni nanocristalli all'avanguardia contengono distribuzioni in dimensioni di particelle e morfologia che limitano le loro prestazioni ottiche.

Due classi di nanocristalli semiconduttori sono state scoperte come eccezioni a questa regola. Essi mostrano una forma insolita di crescita "discreta", saltando tra una serie di dimensioni specifiche. In particolare, i nanocristalli "magici" crescono attraverso una sequenza di dimensioni ben definite. Questa osservazione suggerisce che possono essere possibili nanocristalli con dimensioni eccezionalmente precise.

Lo scopo centrale di questo progetto è quello di determinare come i nanocristalli di dimensioni magiche individuali si avvicinano alla perfezione su scala atomica e come la loro dimensione, forma, composizione, chimica superficiale e struttura influenzano le loro proprietà ottiche. La microscopia e la spettroscopia monoparticella avanzata saranno utilizzate per scoprire le variazioni nascoste nelle misurazioni convenzionali. La comprensione risultante guiderà la sintesi e l'ottimizzazione dei nanocristalli semiconduttori per applicazioni che richiedono proprietà ottiche altamente uniformi.

Descrizione del lavoro

Lo studente di dottorato caratterizzerà nanocristalli a semiconduttore utilizzando tecniche sperimentali complementari ottiche e strutturali. La messa a fuoco iniziale sarà su nanocristalli di dimensioni magiche CdSe, con il lavoro successivamente espandendosi a nanocristalli di diverse dimensioni, composizioni, trattamenti superficiali e eterostrutture, tra cui nucleo / guscio e nanocristalli InP.

Il progetto studierà come le variazioni delle dimensioni, della forma, della composizione, della chimica superficiale e della struttura influenzano le proprietà ottiche. Ensemble e spettroscopia monoparticella saranno utilizzati per quantificare l'eterogeneità ottica e determinare come i nanocristalli di dimensioni magiche si avvicinano alla perfezione su scala atomica. Le misure esamineranno le proprietà come le reti di emissione, le dinamiche di stato eccitato, le fluttuazioni spettrali e l'idoneità dei nanocristalli selezionati come emettitori monofotonici.

Questi studi ottici saranno completati da una caratterizzazione strutturale avanzata. In particolare, lo studente utilizzerà la microscopia criogenica dell'elettrone e l'analisi monoparticola per determinare le strutture tridimensionali dei nanocristalli semiconduttori con risoluzione quasi atomica o atomica. Gli esperimenti esamineranno la forma nanocristale, compresa la possibile troncazione di nanocristalli di dimensioni magiche tetraedrali, e come varia con dimensioni delle particelle, composizione materiale, trattamento superficiale e procedura di isolamento.

Lo studente di dottorato lavorerà a stretto contatto con i ricercatori responsabili della sintesi nanocristale e della modellazione teorica. Questa interazione è centrale per il progetto: verranno forniti campioni avanzati per misurazioni ottiche e strutturali, mentre i risultati della caratterizzazione guideranno i miglioramenti nella sintesi nanocristale, nel trattamento superficiale e nel controllo strutturale. L'esperienza

descriptionByLocale.de:
Promotionsposition in der experimentellen Charakterisierung von Halbleiternanokristallen

100%, Zürich, befristet

Druck
Druckerzeugnisse

Das Optical Materials Engineering Laboratory (Prof. David J. Norris) in der Abteilung Maschinenbau und Verfahrenstechnik (D-MAVT) der ETH Zürich untersucht Synthese, Wachstum, Struktur und optische Eigenschaften von Nanomaterialien. Unser interdisziplinäres und internationales Team kombiniert Materialchemie, optische Spektroskopie, Elektronenmikroskopie, theoretische Modellierung und numerische Simulation, um Materialien im Nanobereich zu verstehen und zu steuern.

Projekthintergrund

Halbleiterkristallite im Nanometerbereich weisen optische Eigenschaften (z. B. Absorptions- und Emissionsspektren) auf, die stark von ihrer Größe abhängen. Da diese Eigenschaft für die Schaffung abstimmbarer optischer Materialien für optoelektronische Anwendungen von Displays und Infrarotkameras bis hin zu Nanophotonik und Quantentechnologien nützlich ist, wurden chemische Synthesen entwickelt, die Nanokristalle aus verschiedenen Halbleitern herstellen. Die fortschrittlichsten Protokolle sind diejenigen, die zu quasi-sphärischen Teilchen führen (bekannt als kolloidale Quantenpunkte). Selbst Nanokristallproben nach dem neuesten Stand der Technik weisen jedoch Verteilungen in Partikelgröße und Morphologie auf, die ihre optische Leistung einschränken.

Zwei Klassen von Halbleiter-Nanokristallen wurden als Ausnahmen von dieser Regel entdeckt. Sie zeigen eine ungewöhnliche Form des "diskreten" Wachstums und springen zwischen einer Reihe bestimmter Größen. Insbesondere "magisch große" Nanokristalle wachsen durch eine Sequenz von gut definierten Größen. Diese Beobachtung legt nahe, dass Nanokristalle mit außergewöhnlich genauen Abmessungen möglich sein könnten.

Zentrales Ziel dieses Projekts ist es, zu bestimmen, wie eng einzelne magisch dimensionierte Nanokristalle an die Perfektion im atomaren Maßstab herangehen und wie ihre Größe, Form, Zusammensetzung, Oberflächenchemie und Struktur ihre optischen Eigenschaften beeinflussen. Fortschrittliche Einzelteilchenmikroskopie und Spektroskopie werden verwendet, um Variationen aufzudecken, die in herkömmlichen Messungen verborgen sind. Das daraus resultierende Verständnis wird die Synthese und Optimierung von Halbleiter-Nanokristallen für Anwendungen leiten, die sehr einheitliche optische Eigenschaften erfordern.

Stellenbeschreibung

Der Doktorand wird Halbleiter-Nanokristalle mit komplementären optischen und strukturellen experimentellen Techniken charakterisieren. Der erste Schwerpunkt wird auf CdSe-Nanokristallen in magischer Größe liegen, wobei die Arbeit anschließend auf Nanokristalle unterschiedlicher Größe, Zusammensetzungen, Oberflächenbehandlungen und Heterostrukturen, einschließlich Kern-/Schale- und InP-Nanokristalle, ausgeweitet wird.

Das Projekt wird untersuchen, wie Variationen in Nanokristallgröße, -form, -zusammensetzung, Oberflächenchemie und -struktur die optischen Eigenschaften beeinflussen. Ensemble- und Einzelpartikelspektroskopie werden verwendet, um die optische Heterogenität zu quantifizieren und zu bestimmen, wie nah magisch große Nanokristalle an die Perfektion im atomaren Maßstab herangehen. Die Messungen werden Eigenschaften wie Emissionslinienbreiten, angeregte Zustandsdynamik, spektrale Schwankungen und die Eignung ausgewählter Nanokristalle als Einzelphotonenemitter untersuchen.

Diese optischen Untersuchungen werden durch eine erweiterte strukturelle Charakterisierung ergänzt. Insbesondere wird der Student kryogene Elektronenmikroskopie und Einzelpartikelanalyse verwenden, um die dreidimensionalen Strukturen von Halbleiternanokristallen mit einer Auflösung im nahen Atom- oder Atommaßstab zu bestimmen. Die Experimente werden die Nanokristallform untersuchen, einschließlich der möglichen Verkürzung tetraedrischer Nanokristalle in magischer Größe und wie sie sich mit der Partikelgröße, der Materialzusammensetzung, der Oberflächenbehandlung und dem Isolationsverfahren unterscheidet.

Der Doktorand wird eng mit Forschern zusammenarbeiten, die für die Nanokristallsynthese und die theoretische Modellierung verantwortlich sind. Diese Wechselwirkung ist für das Projekt von zentraler Bedeutung: fortschrittliche Proben werden für optische und strukturelle Messungen geliefert, während die Charakterisierungsergebnisse Verbesserungen in der Nanokristallsynthese, Oberflächenbehandlung und Strukturkontrolle leiten werden. descriptionByLocale.fr:
Position au doctorat dans la caractérisation expérimentale des nanocristaux semi-conducteurs

100%, Zurich, durée déterminée

imprimer
Drucken

Le Laboratoire d'ingénierie des matériaux optiques (Prof. David J. Norris) du Département d'ingénierie mécanique et des procédés (D-MAVT) de l'ETH Zurich étudie la synthèse, la croissance, la structure et les propriétés optiques des nanomatériaux. Notre équipe interdisciplinaire et internationale combine la chimie des matériaux, la spectroscopie optique, la microscopie électronique, la modélisation théorique et la simulation numérique pour comprendre et contrôler les matériaux à l'échelle nanométrique.

Contexte du projet

Les cristaux semi-conducteurs à l'échelle du nanomètre présentent des propriétés optiques (p. ex. spectres d'absorption et d'émission) qui dépendent fortement de leur taille. Comme cette propriété est utile pour créer des matériaux optiques compatibles pour des applications optoélectroniques allant des écrans et des caméras infrarouges aux nanophotoniques et aux technologies quantiques, des synthèses chimiques ont été développées pour produire des nanocristaux à partir de divers semi-conducteurs. Les protocoles les plus avancés sont ceux qui conduisent à des particules quasi-sphériques (appelées points quantiques colloïdaux). Cependant, même les nanocristaux les plus modernes contiennent des distributions de granulométrie et de morphologie qui limitent leur performance optique.

Deux classes de nanocristaux semi-conducteurs ont été découvertes comme exceptions à cette règle. Ils présentent une forme inhabituelle de croissance « discrète », sautant entre une série de tailles spécifiques. En particulier, les nanocristaux de taille "magique" se développent à travers une séquence de tailles bien définies. Cette observation suggère que des nanocristaux aux dimensions particulièrement précises peuvent être possibles.

Le but principal de ce projet est de déterminer dans quelle mesure les nanocristaux de taille magique individuelle approchent la perfection à l'échelle atomique et comment leur taille, forme, composition, chimie de surface et structure influencent leurs propriétés optiques. La microscopie et la spectroscopie à particules simples seront utilisées pour découvrir les variations qui sont cachées dans les mesures conventionnelles. La compréhension qui en résultera guidera la synthèse et l'optimisation des nanocristaux semi-conducteurs pour des applications nécessitant des propriétés optiques très uniformes.

Description du poste

Le doctorant caractérisera les nanocristaux semi-conducteurs en utilisant des techniques expérimentales optiques et structurelles complémentaires. L'accent initial sera mis sur les nanocristaux de la taille magique du CdSe, les travaux s'étendant ensuite aux nanocristaux de différentes tailles, compositions, traitements de surface et hétérostructures, y compris les nanocristaux de noyau/coque et InP.

Le projet étudiera comment les variations de la taille, de la forme, de la composition, de la chimie de surface et de la structure des nanocristaux influencent les propriétés optiques. L'ensemble et la spectroscopie monoparticulaire serviront à quantifier l'hétérogénéité optique et à déterminer dans quelle mesure les nanocristaux de taille magique approchent la perfection à l'échelle atomique. Les mesures permettront d'examiner les propriétés telles que les linéarités d'émission, la dynamique de l'état excité, les fluctuations spectrales et la pertinence de certains nanocristaux en tant qu'émetteurs monophotons.

Ces études optiques seront complétées par une caractérisation structurale avancée. En particulier, l'étudiant utilisera la microscopie électronique cryogénique et l'analyse monoparticulaire pour déterminer les structures tridimensionnelles des nanocristaux semi-conducteurs à résolution quasi-atomique ou atomique. Les expériences porteront sur la forme des nanocristaux, y compris la possibilité de tronquer les nanocristaux de taille magique tétraédrique, et la façon dont ils varient selon la taille des particules, la composition des matériaux, le traitement de surface et la procédure d'isolement.

Le doctorant travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les chercheurs responsables de la synthèse nanocristale et de la modélisation théorique. Cette interaction est au cœur du projet : des échantillons avancés seront fournis pour des mesures optiques et structurales, tandis que les résultats de caractérisation orienteront les améliorations dans la synthèse nanocristalle, le traitement de surface et le contrôle structural. jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Researcher - Neurostimulation for Stroke Rehabilitation

100%, Singapore, fixed-term

Drucken

The Singapore-ETH Centre was established in 2010 by ETH Zurich - The Swiss Federal Institute of Technology and Singapore’s National Research Foundation (NRF), as part of the NRF’s CREATE campus. As ETH Zurich's only research centre outside of Switzerland, the centre has strengthened the research capacity of ETH Zurich to develop sustainable solutions to global challenges in Switzerland, Singapore and the surrounding regions.

Set in Asia, in a rapidly urbanising region, the Singapore-ETH Centre aims to provide practical solutions to some of the most pressing challenges on urban sustainability, resilience and health through its programmes: Future Cities Lab Global (FCL Global) and Future Health Technologies (FHT) .

The centre serves as an intellectual hub for research, bringing together principal investigators and researchers from diverse disciplines and backgrounds. To promote the exchange of ideas and expertise, our researchers actively collaborate with universities and research institutes and engage with industry and government agencies to translate knowledge to practical solutions to real-world problems.

Project background

Stroke remains a leading cause of disability worldwide. Although improved early stroke response has reduced mortality, it has also produced a growing population of stroke survivors, intensifying the demand for long-term rehabilitation and placing a substantial clinical and economic burden on healthcare systems. Because today’s neurorehabilitation model relies heavily on resource-intensive, therapist-led care, meeting this demand will require scalable, cost-effective solutions that extend beyond the clinic and into the home. To address these needs, the first phase of the Future Health Technologies Programme (FHT1) at the Singapore-ETH Centre (SEC) (https://fht.ethz.ch) developed and piloted innovative upper limb rehabilitation technologies and evaluated them in clinical settings, both in hospital and in the homes of post-stroke subjects. Building on this foundation, FHT2 aims to scale up these technologies and carry out more extensive clinical evaluation, paving the way for technology-based clinic-to-home rehabilitation to be integrated into Singapore’s healthcare system.

Another limitation of conventional rehabilitation is that it rarely addresses the root cause of impairment directly: the injured brain and its motor and sensory pathways. Research has shown that rehabilitation can be made more efficient by using neurostimulation to drive specific patterns of brain activity, and one promising, scalable approach is transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS), which stimulates the auricular branch of the vagus nerve (VN) at the outer ear in a safe, non-invasive way. In close collaboration with the spin-off Skaaltec, the Rehabilitation Engineering Laboratory of ETH Zurich has developed SmartVNS (https://relab.ethz.ch/spin-off/skaaltec.html), a novel system for automated, movement-paired taVNS. SmartVNS pairs a wrist-worn motion tracker with a shoulder-worn stimulator over a wireless link: it autonomously processes arm-movement data and delivers taVNS through a custom-built earpiece electrode at precisely the right moments, promoting well-timed, short-term neuroplasticity.

Within FHT2, this project pursues three objectives: (i) to further explore the mechanistic effects of taVNS and optimise stimulation parameters and timing for maximal response in post-stroke subjects; (ii) to demonstrate the feasibility and clinical applicability of automated, movement-paired taVNS built on the SmartVNS system; and (iii) to investigate the clinical potential of taVNS as a rehabilitation intervention for stroke patients, first in a clinical environment during conventional therapy and later at home, in combination with robotic technologies developed within FHT2.

jobs.description:
Spezialist:in Arbeitssicherheit und Gesundheitsschutz (m/w/d)

80%-100%, Zürich, unbefristet

print
Drucken

Die Abteilung Sicherheit, Gesundheit und Umwelt (SGU) berät, unterstützt und schult sämtliche Organisationseinheiten und Angehörigen der ETH Zürich bei Fragen zu Sicherheit und Gesundheit am Arbeitsplatz. Sie ist Anlaufstelle für alle zentral zu organisierenden Massnahmen im Umgang mit Gefährdungen und Risiken zum Schutz von Mensch, Tier, Sachwerten, Infrastruktur und Umwelt sowie bei Fragen bezüglich der Erfüllung der entsprechenden gesetzlichen Anforderungen. Für den Ereignisfall unterhält sie eine angemessene Notfallorganisation. Sowohl im Alltag als auch im Ereignisfall arbeitet sie eng mit den Behörden und externen Einsatzkräften zusammen.

SGU stellt den systematischen Beizug von ASA-Spezialist:innen gemäss EKAS-Richtlinie 6508 für die ETH sicher. Um diese Aufgabe professionell und effizient erfüllen zu können, suchen wir ab sofort oder nach Vereinbarung eine erfahrene und engagierte Persönlichkeit als Spezialist:in Arbeitssicherheit und Gesundheitsschutz (m/w/d).

Stellenbeschreibung

Bereit für den nächsten Karriereschritt in der Arbeitssicherheit?

Du hast ein gutes Gespür für Sicherheit, liebst es, komplexe Themen verständlich zu machen, und willst mit deinem Know-how wirklich etwas bewegen? Dann bist du bei uns genau richtig.

• Als Teil des «ASA-Teams» der Sektion Arbeitssicherheit, Gesundheit und Umwelt bist du zentrale Ansprechperson für alle Fragen rund um Arbeitssicherheit und Gesundheitsschutz an der ETH Zürich

• Du berätst unsere Organisationseinheiten mit Fachwissen, Empathie und Weitblick – und das nicht nur vom Schreibtisch aus

• Ob Labor, Werkstatt oder Feldarbeit: Du bist mittendrin, wenn es darum geht, Sicherheit mit Innovation zu verbinden

• Du arbeitest eng mit einem interdisziplinären Team zusammen und bringst deine Expertise in Laborsicherheit gezielt ein

• Dabei entwickelst du Sicherheitskonzepte, führst Begehungen durch, schulst Mitarbeitende und findest pragmatische Lösungen – immer mit dem Ziel, Mensch, Umwelt und Infrastruktur bestmöglich zu schützen

• Deine Arbeit ist geprägt von Eigenverantwortung, Dialog und dem Anspruch, gemeinsam besser zu werden

• Dein Arbeitsplatz ist in Zürich, zeitweise bist du aber auch an anderen Standorten der ETH tätig

Profil

• Abgeschlossene naturwissenschaftliche Ausbildung, z.B. Chemie, Biologie

• ASA-Spezialist:in mit eidgenössischem Fachausweis

• Mehrjährige Erfahrung im Laborumfeld mit sehr guten Kenntnissen im Bereich Laborsicherheit und Chemiesicherheit

• Interessiert, dich in weiteren Fachthemen weiterzubilden (z.B. Strahlenschutz, Biosicherheit)

• Freude an kontinuierlicher fachlicher Weiterentwicklung

• Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse, gute Englischkenntnisse (Niveau C1) und starke Kommunikationsfähigkeiten

Arbeitsort

Wir bieten

Werde Teil der ETH Zürich, die nicht nur deine berufliche Entwicklung unterstützt, sondern auch aktiv zu positiven Veränderungen in der Gesellschaft beiträgt.

Arbeiten beim Vizepräsidium für Infrastruktur und Nachhaltigkeit (VPIN) bedeutet, die Zukunft der ETH Zürich aktiv mitzugestalten - eine inspirierende, internationale und innovative Institution. Dein Engagement schafft beste Voraussetzungen für Exzellenz in Lehre, Forschung, Wissenstransfer und Nachhaltigkeit der ETH Zürich.

In einer offenen, inspirierenden Atmosphäre bilden Vertrauen, Verlässlichkeit und gegenseitiger Respekt das Fundament unserer Zusammenarbeit. Wir bieten dir nicht nur Sicherheit, sondern auch vielfältige Weiterentwicklungsmöglichkeiten. Bei uns erwartet dich eine sinnstiftende Arbeit in einem innovativen und wertschätzenden Umfeld, das du mitgesta

descriptionByLocale.it:
Specialista: in sicurezza e protezione della salute sul lavoro (m/f/d)

80%-100%, Zurigo, permanente

Stampato
Stampa

Il Dipartimento della Sicurezza, della Salute e dell'Ambiente (SGU) consiglia, sostiene e forma tutte le unità organizzative e i membri dell'ETH di Zurigo su questioni relative alla sicurezza e alla salute sul lavoro. È il punto di contatto per tutte le misure organizzate centralmente nell'affrontare i pericoli e i rischi per la protezione delle persone, degli animali, delle proprietà, delle infrastrutture e dell'ambiente, nonché per le questioni relative all'adempimento dei requisiti giuridici corrispondenti. In caso di incidente, essa deve mantenere un'adeguata organizzazione di emergenza. Sia nella vita quotidiana che in caso di incidente, funziona a stretto contatto con le autorità e le forze esterne.

SGU assicura l'inclusione sistematica di specialisti ASA in conformità con la guida EKAS 6508 per l'ETH. Al fine di poter svolgere questo compito in modo professionale ed efficiente, siamo alla ricerca di una personalità esperta e impegnata come specialista: nella sicurezza del lavoro e nella protezione della salute (m/f/d).

Descrizione del lavoro

Pronta per il prossimo passo di carriera nella sicurezza del lavoro?

Hai un buon senso di sicurezza, l'amore per rendere gli argomenti complessi comprensibili e davvero vogliono fare la differenza con il tuo know-how? Allora hai ragione con noi.

• Nell’ambito del “gruppo ASA” della Sezione Sicurezza, Salute e Ambiente, sei il referente centrale per tutte le questioni relative alla sicurezza e alla tutela della salute sul lavoro a Zurigo.

• Si consiglia alle nostre unità organizzative con competenza, empatia e vista – e non solo dalla scrivania

• Che si tratti di laboratorio, workshop o lavori sul campo: sei nel mezzo di unire la sicurezza all'innovazione

• Lavori a stretto contatto con un team interdisciplinare e utilizzi la tua esperienza nella sicurezza di laboratorio

• In questo modo, si sviluppano concetti di sicurezza, effettuano visite, addestrano i dipendenti e trovano soluzioni pragmatiche – sempre con l'obiettivo di proteggere le persone, l'ambiente e le infrastrutture nel modo migliore possibile.

• Il vostro lavoro è caratterizzato dalla responsabilità personale, dal dialogo e dall'aspirazione a migliorare insieme

• Il tuo posto di lavoro è a Zurigo, ma a volte lavori anche in altre sedi ETH

Profilo

• Formazione scientifica completata, ad esempio chimica, biologia

• Specialista ASA: in con certificato svizzero

• Diversi anni di esperienza nell'ambiente di laboratorio con ottime conoscenze nel campo della sicurezza di laboratorio e della sicurezza chimica

descriptionByLocale.en:
Specialist: in occupational safety and health protection (m/f/d)

80%-100%, Zurich, permanent

Printed
Printing

The Department of Safety, Health and Environment (SGU) advises, supports and trains all organizational units and members of ETH Zurich on questions relating to safety and health at work. It is the point of contact for all centrally organized measures in dealing with hazards and risks for the protection of people, animals, property, infrastructure and the environment as well as for questions regarding the fulfilment of the corresponding legal requirements. In the event of an incident, it shall maintain an appropriate emergency organisation. Both in everyday life and in the event of an incident, it works closely with the authorities and external forces.

SGU ensures the systematic inclusion of ASA specialists in accordance with EKAS guideline 6508 for the ETH. In order to be able to perform this task professionally and efficiently, we are looking for an experienced and committed personality as a specialist: in occupational safety and health protection (m/f/d).

Job description

Ready for the next career step in occupational safety?

You have a good sense of security, love to make complex topics understandable and really want to make a difference with your know-how? Then you are exactly right with us.

• As part of the “ASA team” of the Occupational Safety, Health and Environment Section, you are the central contact person for all questions relating to occupational safety and health protection at ETH Zurich.

• You advise our organizational units with expertise, empathy and foresight – and not only from the desk

• Whether laboratory, workshop or field work: You are right in the middle of combining security with innovation

• You work closely with an interdisciplinary team and use your expertise in laboratory safety

• In doing so, you develop security concepts, carry out visits, train employees and find pragmatic solutions – always with the aim of protecting people, the environment and infrastructure in the best possible way.

• Your work is characterized by personal responsibility, dialogue and the aspiration to become better together

• Your workplace is in Zurich, but at times you also work at other ETH locations

Profile

• Completed scientific training, e.g. chemistry, biology

• ASA specialist: in with Swiss certificate

• Several years of experience in the laboratory environment with very good knowledge in the field of laboratory safety and chemical safety

• Interested in further training in other specialist topics (e.g. radiation protection, biosecurity)

• Enjoyment of continuous professional development

• Very good knowledge of German, good knowledge of English (level C1) and strong communication skills

Place of work

We offer

Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive changes in society.

Working for the Vice President of Infrastructure and Sustainability (VPIN) means actively shaping the future of ETH Zurich – an inspiring, international and innovative institution. Your commitment creates the best conditions for excellence in teaching, research, knowledge transfer and sustainability at ETH Zurich.

In an open and inspiring atmosphere, trust, reliability and mutual respect form the foundation of our cooperation. We not only offer you security, but also a wide range of further development opportunities. With us, a meaningful work awaits you in an innovative and appreciative environment that you share with us.

Research Assistants (Law, Computer Science, or related fields)

10%-30%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

As part of the SNSF-funded project “Responsible AI for the Swiss Judiciary”, we work on real-world applications of artificial intelligence for the Swiss judiciary in close collaboration with courts and partners across Switzerland. We are looking for Research Assistants (Law, Computer Science, or related fields).

Job description

We are looking for highly motivated Research Assistants to support our SNSF-funded research project.

The position offers a wide range of possible contributions, depending on your background and interests. Tasks may include:

• Supporting stakeholder interactions, including communication and collaboration with courts and judicial actors

• Assisting in the organization and coordination of project activities

• Contributing to project management tasks (e.g., documentation, coordination, project website)

• Supporting the development and refinement of AI-based research prototypes

• Assisting in research activities

This flexibility allows candidates to engage with the project in ways that best match their skills and interests.

Our offices are located in downtown Zurich, and the working languages are German and English.

Profile

We are looking for students enrolled at a Swiss university who are enthusiastic about contributing to an interdisciplinary research project on AI in the judiciary.

We particularly welcome candidates with a background in:

• Law, especially with an interest in AI and judicial processes

• Computer Science or Data Science, especially with practical programming experience

• Currently enrolled as a student at a Swiss university

We are also open to candidates from other disciplines who demonstrate a strong motivation to contribute to our project.

• Experience with project management and German language skills are a plus.

Workplace

We offer

• Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

• You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

We look forward to receiving your online application, including:

Im Rahmen des vom SNF geförderten Projekts „Responsible AI for the Swiss Judiciary arbeiten wir in enger Zusammenarbeit mit Gerichten und Partnern in der ganzen Schweiz an realen Anwendungen künstlicher Intelligenz für die Schweizer Justiz. Wir suchen Forschungsassistenten (Recht, Informatik oder verwandte Bereiche).

Wir suchen hochmotivierte wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiter, die unser vom SNF gefördertes Forschungsprojekt unterstützen.

Die Position bietet eine breite Palette von möglichen Beiträgen, abhängig von Ihrem Hintergrund und Interessen. Zu den Aufgaben können gehören:

• Unterstützung der Interaktionen mit Interessengruppen, einschließlich Kommunikation und Zusammenarbeit mit Gerichten und Justizakteuren

• Unterstützung bei der Organisation und Koordination der Projektaktivitäten

• Unterstützung bei Forschungsaktivitäten

Diese Flexibilität ermöglicht es den Kandidaten, sich auf eine Weise mit dem Projekt zu beschäftigen, die ihren Fähigkeiten und Interessen am besten entspricht.

Wir suchen Studierende einer Schweizer Universität, die sich für ein interdisziplinäres Forschungsprojekt zum Thema KI in der Justiz begeistern.

• Recht, insbesondere mit Interesse an KI und Gerichtsprozessen

jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Researcher (OCCL)

100%, Singapore, fixed-term

Drucken

The Singapore-ETH Centre was established in 2010 by ETH Zurich - The Swiss Federal Institute of Technology and Singapore’s National Research Foundation (NRF), as part of the NRF’s CREATE campus. As ETH Zurich's only research centre outside of Switzerland, the centre has strengthened the research capacity of ETH Zurich to develop sustainable solutions to global challenges in Switzerland, Singapore and the surrounding regions.

Set in Asia, in a rapidly urbanising region, the Singapore-ETH Centre aims to provide practical solutions to some of the most pressing challenges on urban sustainability, resilience and health through its programmes: Future Cities Lab Global (FCL Global) and Future Health Technologies (FHT) .

The centre serves as an intellectual hub for research, bringing together principal investigators and researchers from diverse disciplines and backgrounds. To promote the exchange of ideas and expertise, our researchers actively collaborate with universities and research institutes and engage with industry and government agencies to translate knowledge to practical solutions to real-world problems.

Project background

The current era of artificial intelligence is predominantly driven by advances in computational power and infrastructure. As models scale to unprecedented sizes, their capabilities are enhanced through strategies such as reinforcement learning (RL) and innovative frameworks like the "graph of thoughts". We are firmly in the "Age of Computation", where breakthroughs in AI are synonymous with the ability to harness and optimize massive computational resources. However, this rapid growth in computational demands comes with a critical challenge: energy limitations. Around the globe, new power plants are being constructed to meet the demands of AI workloads, underscoring the urgent need for efficiency to ensure these advancements benefit humanity sustainably. Especially in Singapore, such resources may be scarce and hinder the ability of the country’s researchers to advance in this most important field.

Our collaborative efforts with the A*STAR Institute of Advanced Intelligence and Computing (ASTAR IAIC) and other partners in Singapore, such as NTU, could be pivotal in this field, driving the development and implementation of innovative AI methods and saving millions of dollars in compute time while accelerating scientific productivity. To enhance the efficacy of AI for Science models, it is imperative to integrate simulations that encode prior scientific knowledge within these AI frameworks. This integration is aimed at creating new models imbued with robust prior knowledge, such as simulated behaviors defined by fundamental equations and conservation laws. Our approach involves the close collaboration of experts from A*STAR IAIC, who bring extensive experience in high-performance computing and AI-driven scientific research. jobs.description:
Doctoral Position in topochemical tuning of layered oxides

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The newly established Solid-State Materials Chemistry Group at the Laboratory of Inorganic Chemistry, Department of Chemistry and Applied Biosciences (D-CHAB), ETH Zurich, is seeking a highly motivated Doctoral Position.

Our research investigates how crystal chemistry, structure, and dimensionality can be used to control and create functionality in complex inorganic solids. We are currently establishing a laboratory for thin-film synthesis using physical vapor deposition methods, structural modification using wet-chemistry-based approaches, and advanced structural and functional characterization. Our long-term goal is to develop materials with potential for technology transfer to semiconductor and photonic industries, as well as energy conversion and storage applications.

Project background

Low-temperature chemical reactions (i.e., soft-chemistry) can drive topochemical transformations that modify the composition and structure of an existing solid while preserving its overall crystal framework. Layered perovskite oxides are particularly suited to this approach because their interlayer regions are chemically accessible, while the functional perovskite-derived slabs can remain intact. Changing the interlayer chemistry can alter crystal symmetry, give rise to charge discontinuities and structural distortions, providing a way to control functionality in solids, e.g. magnetic order, ferroelectric polarization configuration, electronic and ionic transport.

In this experimental Doctoral project, you will develop topochemical modifications of functional layered perovskites, working primarily with thin films and, where appropriate, single crystals and nanoparticles. Post-synthetic tuning, such as ion exchange, intercalation, redox reactions, will be used to access reversible property changes that are difficult to obtain by conventional high-temperature synthesis. The broader aim is to establish how topochemical transformations can reconfigure distinct electronic, magnetic, and dipolar states, enabling on-demand functionality for future memory, logic, and sensing applications.

Job description

• Preparing layered oxide precursors as thin films (pulsed-laser deposition), single crystals (e.g., floating zone method) or nanoparticles (e.g., hydrothermal synthesis)

• Developing post-growth topochemical reactions using solution-based and controlled-atmosphere methods

• Following changes in composition, structure, and functional properties using X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, scanning-probe microscopy, magnetometry, and electrical measurements, as well as experiments at large-scale facilities (e.g., Paul Scherrer Institute)

• Presenting your results at scientific conferences, publishing your work, and collaborating with researchers within the group and internationally

Profile

• You should hold a master’s degree in chemistry, materials science, physics or a related field and have a foundation in inorganic materials synthesis

• We are looking for a highly motivated, curious, and self-driven researcher who would be enthusiastic about helping establish a new laboratory: contributing to the installation of equipment, establishing safe and reproducible synthetic procedures, and helping create a collaborative group culture

• Excellent spoken and written English

• Willingness to work in an international and diverse team

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be advantageous, but not required: inorganic or solid-state synthesis, solution-based and soft-chemical methods, hydrothermal or solvothermal synthesis, thin-film deposition, single-crystal synthesis, scanning probe microscopy, electron microscopy, Raman spectroscopy, electrical transport measurements.

Workplace

We offer

• A fully funded doctoral position for four years with a competitive salary according to ETH standards

descriptionByLocale.it:
Posizione di dottorato in topochimica di ossidi strati

100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato

stampa
Druppo

Il nuovo Gruppo di Chimica Solid-State Materials presso il Laboratorio di Chimica Inorganica, Dipartimento di Chimica e Bioscienze Applicate (D-CHAB), ETH Zurich, sta cercando una posizione Dottorale altamente motivata.

La nostra ricerca indaga su come la chimica cristallina, la struttura e la dimensionalità possono essere utilizzate per controllare e creare funzionalità in solidi inorganici complessi. Stiamo attualmente creando un laboratorio per la sintesi di film sottile utilizzando metodi di deposizione del vapore fisico, modifiche strutturali utilizzando approcci basati su chimica bagnata e caratterizzazione strutturale e funzionale avanzata. Il nostro obiettivo a lungo termine è quello di sviluppare materiali con potenziale per il trasferimento di tecnologia a semiconduttori e industrie fotoniche, così come la conversione di energia e applicazioni di storage.

Sfondo del progetto

Le reazioni chimiche a bassa temperatura (cioè, soft-chemistry) possono guidare trasformazioni topochimiche che modificano la composizione e la struttura di un solido esistente mantenendo il suo quadro generale di cristallo. Gli ossidi di perovskite stratificato sono particolarmente adatti a questo approccio perché le loro regioni interstrato sono chimicamente accessibili, mentre le lastre funzionali derivate da perovskite possono rimanere integre. Cambiare la chimica interstrato può alterare la simmetria di cristallo, dare origine a discontinuità di carica e distorsioni strutturali, fornendo un modo per controllare la funzionalità in solidi, ad esempio ordine magnetico, configurazione di polarizzazione ferroe, trasporto elettronico e ionico.

In questo progetto sperimentale di dottorato, svilupperai modifiche topochimiche di perovskite funzionali a strati, lavorando principalmente con film sottili e, se del caso, singoli cristalli e nanoparticelle. La sintonizzazione post-sintetica, come scambio ionico, intercalazione, reazioni redox, sarà utilizzata per accedere a cambiamenti di proprietà reversibili che sono difficili da ottenere dalla sintesi ad alta temperatura convenzionale. L'obiettivo più ampio è quello di stabilire come le trasformazioni chimiche possono riconfigurare stati elettronici, magnetici e dipolari distinti, consentendo funzionalità on-demand per future applicazioni di memoria, logica e rilevamento.

Descrizione del lavoro

• Preparare i precursori dell'ossido stratificato come film sottili (deposizione del laser), cristalli singoli (ad esempio, metodo della zona galleggiante) o nanoparticelle (ad esempio, sintesi idrotermica)

• Sviluppo di reazioni topochimiche post-crescita utilizzando metodi basati su soluzioni e controllati dell'atmosfera

• A seguito di cambiamenti nella composizione, nella struttura e nelle proprietà funzionali utilizzando la diffrazione a raggi X, la spettroscopia Raman, la microscopia a scansione, la magnetometria e le misurazioni elettriche, nonché gli esperimenti in impianti su larga scala (ad esempio, Paul Scherrer Institute)

• Presentare i tuoi risultati in conferenze scientifiche, pubblicare il tuo lavoro e collaborare con i ricercatori all'interno del gruppo e a livello internazionale

Profilo

• Si dovrebbe tenere un master in chimica, scienza dei materiali, fisica o un campo correlato e avere una base in sintesi dei materiali inorganici

• Siamo alla ricerca di un ricercatore altamente motivato, curioso e self-driven che sarebbe entusiasta di contribuire a creare un nuovo laboratorio: contribuire all'installazione di attrezzature, stabilire procedure sintetiche sicure e riproducibili, e contribuire a creare una cultura di gruppo collaborativa

• Ottimo parlato e scritto inglese

• Volontà di lavorare in un team internazionale e diversificato

L'esperienza in una o più delle seguenti aree sarebbe vantaggiosa, ma non necessaria: sintesi inorganica o a stato solido, metodi soluzione-basati e soft-chimici, sintesi idrotermale o solvotermale, deposizione di film sottile, sintesi monocristallino, microscopia della sonda di scansione, microscopia elettronica, spettroscopia Raman, misure di trasporto elettrico.

Luogo di lavoro

Offriamo

• Una posizione di dottorato completamente finanziata per quattro anni con uno stipendio competitivo secondo gli standard ETH

Post-synthetic tuning, such as ion exchange, intercalation, redox reactions, will be used to access reversible property changes that are difficult to obtain by conventional high-temperature synthesis. Unsere Forschung untersucht, wie Kristallchemie, Struktur und Dimensionalität verwendet werden können, um Funktionalität in komplexen anorganischen Feststoffen zu steuern und zu erzeugen. Wir errichten derzeit ein Labor für die Dünnschichtsynthese mit physikalischen Dampfabscheidungsmethoden, strukturelle Modifikation mit nasschemischen Ansätzen und fortschrittliche strukturelle und funktionelle Charakterisierung. Chemische Niedertemperaturreaktionen (d.h. Weichchemie) können topochemische Transformationen vorantreiben, die die Zusammensetzung und Struktur eines vorhandenen Feststoffs verändern und gleichzeitig seinen gesamten Kristallrahmen erhalten. 100%, Zurich, durée déterminée

imprimer
Purée

Le nouveau Solid-State Materials Chemistry Group au Laboratoire de chimie inorganique, Département de chimie et de biosciences appliquées (D-CHAB), ETH Zurich, cherche un poste de doctorat hautement motivé.

Notre recherche examine comment la chimie cristalline, la structure et la dimensionnalité peuvent être utilisées pour contrôler et créer des fonctionnalités dans des solides inorganiques complexes. Nous établissons actuellement un laboratoire de synthèse des films minces à l'aide de méthodes de dépôt de vapeurs physiques, de modifications structurelles à l'aide d'approches fondées sur la chimie humide et de caractérisations structurales et fonctionnelles avancées. Notre objectif à long terme est de développer des matériaux susceptibles d'être transférés à des industries de semi-conducteurs et de photonique, ainsi que des applications de conversion et de stockage d'énergie.

Contexte du projet

Les réactions chimiques à basse température (c.-à-d. la chimie douce) peuvent entraîner des transformations topochimiques qui modifient la composition et la structure d'un solide existant tout en préservant son cadre cristallin global. Les oxydes de perovskite en couches sont particulièrement adaptés à cette approche parce que leurs régions intercouches sont chimiquement accessibles, tandis que les dalles fonctionnelles de perovskite peuvent rester intactes. Changer la chimie intercouche peut modifier la symétrie cristalline, donner lieu à des discontinuités de charge et des distorsions structurelles, fournissant un moyen de contrôler la fonctionnalité dans les solides, par exemple l'ordre magnétique, la configuration de polarisation ferroélectrique, le transport électronique et ionique.

Dans ce projet expérimental Doctoral, vous développerez des modifications topochimiques des perovskites en couches fonctionnelles, travaillant principalement avec des films minces et, le cas échéant, des cristaux uniques et des nanoparticules. Le réglage post-synthétique, comme l'échange d'ions, l'intercalation, les réactions redox, sera utilisé pour accéder à des changements de propriétés réversibles qui sont difficiles à obtenir par synthèse conventionnelle à haute température. L'objectif plus large est d'établir comment les transformations topochimiques peuvent reconfigurer des états électroniques, magnétiques et dipolaires distincts, permettant la fonctionnalité à la demande pour les applications futures de la mémoire, de la logique et de la détection.

Description de l'emploi

• Préparation de précurseurs d'oxydes stratifiés sous forme de minces films (dépôts de lasers à impulsions), de cristaux simples (par exemple, méthode de zone flottante) ou de nanoparticules (par exemple, synthèse hydrothermale)

• Développement de réactions topochimiques post-croissance à l'aide de méthodes à base de solution et d'atmosphère contrôlée

• À la suite de changements dans la composition, la structure et les propriétés fonctionnelles à l'aide de la diffraction des rayons X, de la spectroscopie Raman, de la microscopie par sonde à balayage, de la magnétométrie et des mesures électriques, ainsi que d'expériences dans des installations à grande échelle (par exemple, l'Institut Paul Scherrer)

• Présenter vos résultats lors de conférences scientifiques, publier vos travaux et collaborer avec des chercheurs du groupe et à l'échelle internationale

Profil

• Vous devriez détenir un master en chimie, science des matériaux, physique ou un domaine connexe et avoir une fondation dans la synthèse des matériaux inorganiques

• Nous sommes à la recherche d'un chercheur très motivé, curieux et autonome qui serait enthousiaste à l'idée d'aider à créer un nouveau laboratoire : contribuer à l'installation d'équipement, établir des procédures synthétiques sûres et reproductibles, et contribuer à créer une culture de groupe collaborative

• Excellent anglais parlé et écrit

• Volonté de travailler dans une équipe internationale et diversifiée

Doctoral Position in functional oxide thin films

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The newly established Solid-State Materials Chemistry Group at the Laboratory of Inorganic Chemistry, Department of Chemistry and Applied Biosciences (D-CHAB), ETH Zurich, is seeking a highly motivated Doctoral Position.

Our research investigates how crystal chemistry, structure, and dimensionality can be used to control and create functionality in complex inorganic solids. We are currently establishing a laboratory for thin-film synthesis using physical vapor deposition methods, structural modification using wet-chemistry-based approaches, and advanced structural and functional characterization. Our long-term goal is to develop materials with potential for technology transfer to semiconductor and photonic industries, as well as energy conversion and storage applications.

Project background

Controlling and coupling electric, magnetic, and structural properties within a single material could open new routes towards low-power electronics. Transition-metal perovskite oxides offer a versatile platform for this purpose: their A- and B-cation chemistry can be varied to tune the interplay between lattice, orbital, spin, and charge degrees of freedom.

In this experimental Doctoral project, you will investigate layered perovskite-based oxides, in which spacer layers interrupt the three-dimensional perovskite network. This lowers the crystal symmetry, introduces strong anisotropy, and promotes structural distortions that couple magnetic and ferroelectric order. In epitaxial thin films, strain and interfaces offer additional ways to engineer these properties.

Job description

• Growing epitaxial thin films and heterostructures by pulsed-laser deposition and magnetron sputtering and using epitaxial strain and interfacial effects to stabilize metastable phases with desired structural, electronic, and magnetic functionality.

• Thin-film structural and functional characterization using X-ray diffraction, scanning-probe microscopy, magnetometry, synchrotron-based experiments (e.g., at Paul Scherrer Institute)

• Fabricating thin-film devices in a cleanroom and performing electrical and transport characterization

• Using first-principles calculations and machine-learning foundation models during the initial stage of the project to identify promising metastable compositions for experimental stabilization as thin films

• Presenting your results at scientific conferences, publishing your work, and collaborating with researchers within the group and internationally

Profile

• You should hold a master’s degree in chemistry, physics, materials science or a related field

• We are looking for a highly motivated, curious, and self-driven researcher, who would be enthusiastic about helping establish a new laboratory: contributing to the installation of equipment, developing reliable experimental protocols and helping create a collaborative group culture

• Excellent spoken and written English

• Willingness to work in an international and diverse team

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be advantageous, but not required: thin-film deposition, solid-state synthesis, crystallography, complex transition-metal oxides, scanning probe microscopy, electrical transport measurements, device fabrication, first-principles material modelling.

Workplace

We offer

• A fully funded doctoral position for four years with a competitive salary according to ETH standards

• Access to a state-of-the-art ultra-high-vacuum thin-film deposition cluster, a laboratory for wet-chemical and solid-state synthesis, and advanced structural and functional characterization facilities

• Excellent training opportunities and employment conditions according to ETH Zurich standards

stampa
Druppo

Il nuovo Gruppo di Chimica Solid-State Materials presso il Laboratorio di Chimica Inorganica, Dipartimento di Chimica e Bioscienze Applicate (D-CHAB), ETH Zurich, sta cercando una posizione Dottorale altamente motivata.

Stiamo attualmente creando un laboratorio per la sintesi di film sottile utilizzando metodi di deposizione del vapore fisico, modifiche strutturali utilizzando approcci basati su chimica bagnata e caratterizzazione strutturale e funzionale avanzata. Il nostro obiettivo a lungo termine è quello di sviluppare materiali con potenziale per il trasferimento di tecnologia a semiconduttori e industrie fotoniche, così come la conversione di energia e applicazioni di storage.

Sfondo del progetto

Controllo e accoppiamento delle proprietà elettriche, magnetiche e strutturali all'interno di un unico materiale potrebbe aprire nuove rotte verso l'elettronica a bassa potenza. Gli ossidi di perovskite transition-metal offrono una piattaforma versatile per questo scopo: la loro chimica A- e B-cation può essere variata per sintonizzare l'interazione tra reticolo, orbitale, spin e gradi di carica di libertà.

In questo progetto sperimentale Doctoral, si indagano ossidi a base di perovskite strati, in cui strati di distanziatore interrompono la rete tridimensionale perovskite. Questo abbassa la simmetria di cristallo, introduce anisotropia forte, e promuove distorsioni strutturali che accoppiano l'ordine magnetico e ferroelettrico. In pellicole sottili epitassiali, varietà e interfacce offrono modi aggiuntivi per progettare queste proprietà.

Descrizione del lavoro

• Crescendo pellicole sottili epitassiali e eterostrutture mediante deposizione a laser pulsato e sputtering del magnetron e utilizzando lo sforzo epitassiale e gli effetti interfacciali per stabilizzare le fasi metastabili con la funzionalità strutturale, elettronica e magnetica desiderata.

• Caratterizzazione strutturale e funzionale del Thin-film utilizzando diffrazione a raggi X, microscopia a scansione-probe, magnetometria, esperimenti basati su sincrotrone (ad esempio, presso Paul Scherrer Institute)

• Realizzazione di dispositivi a film sottile in una stanza pulita e caratterizzazione elettrica e di trasporto

• Utilizzando i calcoli dei primi principi e i modelli di fondazione di machine-learning durante la fase iniziale del progetto per identificare promettenti composizioni metastabili per la stabilizzazione sperimentale come film sottili

• Presentare i tuoi risultati in conferenze scientifiche, pubblicare il tuo lavoro e collaborare con i ricercatori all'interno del gruppo e a livello internazionale

Profilo

• Si dovrebbe tenere un master in chimica, fisica, scienza dei materiali o un campo correlato

• Siamo alla ricerca di un ricercatore altamente motivato, curioso e self-driven, che sarebbe entusiasta di contribuire a creare un nuovo laboratorio: contribuire all'installazione di apparecchiature, sviluppare protocolli sperimentali affidabili e contribuire a creare una cultura di gruppo collaborativa

• Ottimo parlato e scritto inglese

• Volontà di lavorare in un team internazionale e diversificato

L'esperienza in una o più delle seguenti aree sarebbe vantaggiosa, ma non necessaria: deposizione di film sottile, sintesi a stato solido, cristalliografia, ossidi di transizione-metal complessi, microscopia della sonda di scansione, misure di trasporto elettrico, fabbricazione di dispositivi, modellazione di materiali di primo principio.

Luogo di lavoro

Offriamo

• Una posizione di dottorato completamente finanziata per quattro anni con uno stipendio competitivo secondo gli standard ETH

• Accesso a un cluster di deposizione a film sottile ultra-alto-vacuo all'avanguardia, un laboratorio per la sintesi a stato solido e chimico bagnato e strutture di caratterizzazione strutturale e funzionali avanzate

• Ottime opportunità di formazione e condizioni di lavoro secondo gli standard ETH Zurich

• Puoi aspettarti numerosi vantaggi, come i biglietti per la stagione dei trasporti pubblici e la condivisione delle auto, una vasta gamma di sport offerti dall'ASVZ, l'assistenza all'infanzia e la pensione attraente

Contexte du projet

Le contrôle et le couplage des propriétés électriques, magnétiques et structurelles d'un même matériau pourraient ouvrir de nouvelles voies vers l'électronique de faible puissance. Les oxydes perovskite de métaux de transition offrent une plate-forme polyvalente à cette fin : leur chimie de position A et B peut être variée pour régler l'interaction entre le réseau, l'orbite, le spin et les degrés de liberté de charge.

Dans ce projet expérimental Doctoral, vous étudierez les oxydes à base de perovskite en couches, dans lesquelles les couches d'espacement interrompent le réseau de perovskite en trois dimensions. Cela réduit la symétrie cristalline, introduit une forte anisotropie et favorise des distorsions structurelles qui couplent ordre magnétique et ferroélectrique. Dans les films minces épitaxiaux, les déformations et les interfaces offrent d'autres façons d'imaginer ces propriétés.

Description de l'emploi

• La croissance de films minces et d'hétérostructures épitaxiales par dépôt de laser pulsé et par pulvérisation de magnétron et l'utilisation de déformations épitaxiales et d'effets interfaciaux pour stabiliser les phases métastables avec la fonctionnalité structurelle, électronique et magnétique souhaitée.

• Caractérisation structurale et fonctionnelle par diffraction des rayons X, microscopie par sonde à balayage, magnétométrie, expériences à base de synchrotron (p. ex., à l'Institut Paul Scherrer)

• Fabrication d'appareils à film mince dans une salle propre et caractérisation électrique et transport

• Utilisation des calculs des premiers principes et des modèles de base de l'apprentissage automatique au cours de la phase initiale du projet pour identifier les compositions métastables prometteuses pour la stabilisation expérimentale comme films minces

• Présenter vos résultats lors de conférences scientifiques, publier vos travaux et collaborer avec des chercheurs du groupe et à l'échelle internationale

Profil

• Vous devriez détenir un master en chimie, physique, sciences des matériaux ou un domaine connexe

• Nous sommes à la recherche d'un chercheur hautement motivé, curieux et autonome, qui serait enthousiaste à l'idée d'aider à créer un nouveau laboratoire : contribuer à l'installation d'équipement, développer des protocoles expérimentaux fiables et contribuer à créer une culture de groupe collaborative

• Excellent anglais parlé et écrit

• Volonté de travailler dans une équipe internationale et diversifiée

L'expérience dans un ou plusieurs des domaines suivants serait avantageuse, mais non requise : dépôt de film mince, synthèse à l'état solide, cristallographie, oxydes métalliques de transition complexes, microscopie à sonde à balayage, mesures du transport électrique, fabrication d'appareils, modélisation des matériaux des premiers principes.

Lieu de travail

Nous offrons

• Un poste de doctorat entièrement financé pour quatre ans avec un salaire concurrentiel selon les normes ETH

• Accès à un cluster ultra-haut-vacuum ultra-moderne de dépôt de film mince, à un laboratoire de synthèse à l'état humide et solide et à des installations de caractérisation structurale et fonctionnelle avancées

• Excellentes possibilités de formation et conditions d'emploi selon les normes ETH Zurich

• Vous pouvez vous attendre à de nombreux avantages, tels que les billets de saison des transports en commun et le partage de voiture, un large éventail de sports offerts par l'ASVZ, garde d'enfants et une pension attrayante

jobs.description:
Junior Researcher in Public Economics and International Taxation

70%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Swiss Economic Institute (KOF) is seeking a Junior Researcher (Scientific assistants) to support Dr. Enea Baselgia's SNSF-funded research project "Taxation in a Globalized Economy: Profit Shifting, Tax Competition, and the Political Economy of Tax Havens" (70%, one-year fixed-term contract, starting November 1, 2026 or by agreement).

You will be employed at the KOF Swiss Economic Institute at ETH Zurich, which is the leading institute for applied research in economics in Switzerland. KOF has a strong collaborative environment that promotes exchange between research staff at different levels and in different functions and is committed to rigorous, applied research on policy-relevant topics with a connection to Switzerland.

Project background

In collaboration with leading scholars (incl., e.g., Florian Scheuer, Michael Siegenthaler, and Gabriel Zucman, among others), and leveraging exceptionally rich linked Swiss administrative data, the projects aim to generate new causal evidence and insights on multinational profit shifting, corporate tax competition, wealth taxation, and the political economy of tax havens, all questions of central importance to academics and policymakers alike at a time when international coordination on taxation is at a crossroads.

Job description

Your primary tasks will be to support the preparation and analysis of micro-level data underlying the project's research questions. This includes:

• Preparing and managing linked micro-level datasets (cleaning, merging, quality checks)

• Conducting descriptive analyses of administrative and survey data

• Running guided empirical analyses using reduced-form causal inference methods

• Preparing presentation slides and other research materials

• Occasionally assisting in the organization of an academic workshop

Profile

We are looking for an outstanding candidate who is curious, proactive, and enthusiastic about producing rigorous scientific evidence to improve tax policy.

Your profile:

• Completed master's degree in economics, political science, or other quantitative social science

• Genuine interest in policy-relevant questions in taxation and public economics

• Reliable, structured and precise working style

• Very good planning and coordination skills

• Comfortable formulating questions and proactively seeking guidance as needed

• Curious and self-motivated, with a strong sense of ownership over their work

• Solid foundations in causal inference methods (e.g., difference-in-differences, instrumental variables, and randomized experiments)

• Proficiency in the statistical software package Stata and/or R

• Prior experience with large-scale data cleaning and management (is not required but a plus)

• Good command of German and English for this position

• Excellent writing skills in English and German

• Strong interest in applied scientific research (an interest in pursuing a PhD at a later stage is a plus but not necessary)

Workplace

We offer

• Hands-on experience contributing to high-quality academic research and developing your own academic skills

• Highly collaborative work environment: You will be working closely with researchers at different levels and be integrated in a team with other junior and PhD researchers

• Professional supervision by experienced researchers, supporting you in your career development as an applied economist

• Access to a flexible working environment: Opportunities for flexible working hours and a supportive learning environment

• You can look forward to numerous benefits , a wide range of sports activities organised by the ASVZ

• Salary and pension benefits according to ETH regulation

L'Istituto economico svizzero (KOF) sta cercando un ricercatore junior (assistenti scientifici) per sostenere il progetto di ricerca finanziato dalla Dr.ssa Enea Baselgia "Tassazione in un'economia globalizzata: trasferimento di profitti, concorrenza fiscale e economia politica dei paradisi fiscali" (70%, contratto a tempo determinato di un anno, a partire dal 1 novembre 2026 o previo accordo).

Lavora presso l'Istituto svizzero di economia KOF di ETH Zurigo, che è il principale istituto di ricerca applicata in economia in Svizzera. KOF ha un ambiente di forte collaborazione che promuove lo scambio tra ricercatori di diversi livelli e funzioni e si impegna a una ricerca rigorosa e applicata su temi rilevanti in relazione con la Svizzera.

Contesto del progetto

In collaborazione con importanti studiosi (tra cui Florian Scheuer, Michael Siegenthaler e Gabriel Zucman), e sfruttando dati amministrativi svizzeri estremamente ricchi, i progetti mirano a generare nuove prove e approfondimenti causali sul trasferimento degli utili multinazionali, sulla concorrenza fiscale delle imprese, sulla tassazione della ricchezza e sull'economia politica dei paradisi fiscali, tutte questioni di importanza centrale per gli accademici e i politici, in un momento in cui il coordinamento internazionale sulla tassazione è a un bivio.

Descrizione del lavoro

I vostri compiti principali saranno quello di sostenere la preparazione e l'analisi dei dati di microlivello che stanno alla base delle domande di ricerca del progetto.

• Analisi descrittive dei dati amministrativi e di indagine

• Esecuzione di analisi empiriche guidate utilizzando metodi di inferenza causale a forma ridotta

• Preparazione di diapositive di presentazione e altri materiali di ricerca

• Occasionalmente assiste nell'organizzazione di un seminario accademico

• Fondamenti solidi nei metodi di inferenza causale (ad esempio, differenze in-differenza, variabili strumentali ed esperimenti randomizzati)

• Proficienza nel pacchetto di software statistico Stata e/o R

• Precedente esperienza con la pulizia e la gestione dei dati su larga scala (non è necessario ma un plus)

70%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Swiss Economic Institute (KOF) is seeking a Junior Researcher (Scientific assistants) to support Dr. Enea Baselgia's SNSF-funded research project "Taxation in a Globalized Economy: Profit Shifting, Tax Competition, and the Political Economy of Tax Havens" (70%, one-year fixed-term contract, starting November 1, 2026 or by agreement).

You will be employed at the KOF Swiss Economic Institute at ETH Zurich, which is the leading institute for applied research in economics in Switzerland. KOF has a strong collaborative environment that promotes exchange between research staff at different levels and in different functions and is committed to rigorous, applied research on policy-relevant topics with a connection to Switzerland.

Project background

In collaboration with leading scholars (incl., e.g., Florian Scheuer, Michael Siegenthaler, and Gabriel Zucman, among others), and leveraging exceptionally rich linked Swiss administrative data, the projects aim to generate new causal evidence and insights on multinational profit shifting, corporate tax competition, wealth taxation, and the political economy of tax havens, all questions of central importance to academics and policymakers alike at a time when international coordination on taxation is at a crossroads.

Job description

Your primary tasks will be to support the preparation and analysis of micro-level data underlying the project's research questions. This includes:

• Preparing and managing linked micro-level datasets (cleaning, merging, quality checks)

• Conducting descriptive analyses of administrative and survey data

• Running guided empirical analyses using reduced-form causal inference methods

• Preparing presentation slides and other research materials

• Occasionally assisting in the organization of an academic workshop

Profile

We are looking for an outstanding candidate who is curious, proactive, and enthusiastic about producing rigorous scientific evidence to improve tax policy.

Your profile:

• Completed master's degree in economics, political science, or other quantitative social science

• Genuine interest in policy-relevant questions in taxation and public economics

• Reliable, structured and precise working style

• Very good planning and coordination skills

• Comfortable formulating questions and proactively seeking guidance as needed

• Curious and self-motivated, with a strong sense of ownership over their work

• Solid foundations in causal inference methods (e.g., difference-in-differences, instrumental variables, and randomized experiments)

• Proficiency in the statistical software package Stata and/or R

• Prior experience with large-scale data cleaning and management (is not required but a plus)

• Good command of German and English for this position

• Excellent writing skills in English and German

• Strong interest in applied scientific research (an interest in pursuing a PhD at a later stage is a plus but not necessary)

Workplace

We offer

• Hands-on experience contributing to high-quality academic research and developing your own academic skills

• Highly collaborative work environment: You will be working closely with researchers at different levels and be integrated in a team with other junior and PhD researchers

• Professional supervision by experienced researchers, supporting you in your career development as an applied economist

• Access to a flexible working environment: Opportunities for flexible working hours and a supportive learning environment

• You can look forward to numerous benefits , a wide range of sports activities organised by the ASVZ

• Salary and pension benefits according to ETH regulation

L'Institut économique suisse (KOF) cherche un chercheur (assistant scientifique) pour soutenir le projet de recherche financé par la SNSF, intitulé « Taxation in a Globalized Economy: Profit Shifting, Tax Competition, and the Political Economy of Tax Havens » (la fiscalité dans une économie mondialisée : changement de profit, concurrence fiscale et économie politique des paradis fiscaux) (70%, contrat à durée déterminée d'un an, à compter du 1er novembre 2026 ou par accord).

Vous serez employé à l'Institut économique suisse de la KOF à l'ETH Zurich, qui est le principal institut de recherche appliquée en économie en Suisse. KOF a un environnement de collaboration solide qui favorise l'échange entre le personnel de recherche à différents niveaux et dans différentes fonctions et s'engage dans une recherche rigoureuse et appliquée sur des sujets pertinents pour la politique en Suisse.

Contexte du projet

En collaboration avec des chercheurs de premier plan (notamment Florian Scheuer, Michael Siegenthaler et Gabriel Zucman), et en tirant parti de données administratives suisses particulièrement riches, les projets visent à produire de nouvelles preuves causales et de nouvelles idées sur l'évolution des bénéfices multinationaux, la concurrence fiscale des sociétés, la fiscalité de la richesse et l'économie politique des paradis fiscaux, toutes questions d'importance centrale pour les universitaires et les décideurs, alors que la coordination internationale en matière de fiscalité se trouve à la croisée des chemins.

Description du poste

Vos tâches principales seront de soutenir la préparation et l'analyse de données micro-niveaux sous-jacentes aux questions de recherche du projet.

• Préparation et gestion de ensembles de données micro-niveaux liés (nettoyage, fusion, contrôles de qualité)

• Réalisation d'analyses descriptives des données administratives et des enquêtes

• Analyses empiriques guidées utilisant des méthodes d'inférence causale de forme réduite

• Préparation de diapositives de présentation et d'autres documents de recherche

• Aide occasionnelle à l'organisation d'un atelier universitaire

Profil

Nous cherchons un candidat exceptionnel qui est curieux, proactif et enthousiaste à l'idée de produire des preuves scientifiques rigoureuses pour améliorer la politique fiscale.

Votre profil:

• Maîtrise en économie, sciences politiques ou autres sciences sociales quantitatives

• Intérêt véritable pour les questions de politique générale en matière de fiscalité et d'économie publique

• Style de travail fiable, structuré et précis

• Très bonnes compétences en planification et coordination

• Formulation confortable de questions et recherche proactive d'orientations au besoin

• Curieux et automotivé, avec un fort sentiment de propriété sur leur travail

• Fondements solides des méthodes d'inférence causale (par exemple, différences de différences, variables instrumentales et expériences randomisées)

• Compétence du progiciel statistique Stata et/ou R

• Expérience préalable en matière de nettoyage et de gestion des données à grande échelle (pas besoin mais un plus)

• Bonne maîtrise de l'allemand et de l'anglais pour ce poste

• Excellente compétence en écriture en anglais et en allemand

• Intérêt marqué pour la recherche scientifique appliquée (un intérêt pour la poursuite d'un doctorat à un stade ultérieur est un plus mais pas nécessaire)

Travail

jobs.description:
Doctoral Position in Customer-Facing AI in Marketing and Service

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

At the Center for AI Value, part of the Technology Marketing Group at ETH Zurich, we investigate how organisations can turn generative and multimodal AI into measurable value. Our current focus is one of the most consequential open questions in this space: how customer-facing AI should be designed when it speaks to real customers on behalf of a real firm. Generative voice agents now handle substantive service conversations, hand customers over to human employees, and generate content that reaches large professional audiences — yet the design decisions behind them are made largely by intuition.

We are looking for a doctoral candidate to help change that. The position is built around three projects, all of them conducted with industry partners and all of them designed to move from controlled experiments into live operations. You will study how tightly a firm should prescribe what its AI agent says, what happens emotionally and informationally when a conversation is handed from an AI to a human colleague, and how multimodal models can predict the performance of marketing content before it is published.

Research at the Center builds on the group's track record in data science, conversational AI, and marketing analytics and on substantial investments in on-premises GPU infrastructure that allows us to work with confidential partner data under full data control. The focus of the position is on research, aiming at publications in leading international management journals. The starting date is flexible. Applications will be accepted until the position is filled. For further information please refer to Sebastian Tillmanns.

Project background

The position spans three projects, each carried out in close collaboration with an industry partner and each combining controlled experimentation with access to real operational settings. The projects build on established collaborations, ongoing research, and technical infrastructure already in place at the Center.

Prompt granularity in AI voice agents. Firms deploying generative voice agents must decide how tightly to prescribe what the agent says. Tight specification buys reliability, completeness and policy compliance; open specification buys adaptivity to cases nobody anticipated. This project treats that decision as the machine analogue of the classic scripting-versus-empowerment trade-off in service operations — with the crucial difference that script strictness, an aspiration with human employees, becomes an enforceable parameter with a large language model. The programme comprises laboratory experiments with live voice interaction, a comparison of adaptive prompting policies, and a field experiment in the live call operations of a partner in the insurance sector. Outcomes are deliberately behavioural: verified task success, conversational repair derived from transcripts, and compliance failures such as unauthorised commitments.

Emotional grounding in AI-to-human handovers. When a customer in a negative emotional state is transferred from a voice agent to a human employee, does the emotional acknowledgement offered by the AI carry over — or does it retrospectively read as a script if the human does not build on it? This project examines whether the two agents jointly establish common ground about the customer's situation, and how that perceived continuity shapes whether customers feel heard and go on to recommend the provider. It progresses from a factorial experiment through studies with trained actors simulating the handover to a field implementation with the same insurance partner.
