jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Researcher: Experimental Fracture Mechanics of Soft Materials

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

At the Professorship of Solid Mechanics (SMEC) in the Institute for Building Materials at ETH Zurich, we aim to understand how materials deform, degrade, break, and ultimately fail. Our research is driven by curiosity about the physical mechanisms that underlie failure and by the ambition to translate this understanding into more reliable and resilient materials and structures. By combining numerical modeling, laboratory experiments, and theoretical analyses, we seek to link microscopic processes with the macroscopic behavior of both engineering and natural systems and develop predictive tools for mechanical failure.

Our team is highly interdisciplinary and international, bringing together researchers with backgrounds in materials science, mechanics, and applied physics. We work across a broad range of topics, including the mechanics of particle systems (colloidal and granular), architected and topologically interlocked materials, the mechanics of fragility in collagen, the mechanics of earthquakes, fracture of soft materials, and modeling failure in multiphysical processes such as corrosion-driven degradation of concrete. What unites these efforts is a shared curiosity about why complex materials fail and a commitment to developing new concepts, experiments, and models that advance our understanding of failure mechanics.

To expand our research in experimental fracture mechanics, we are seeking a motivated and innovative Postdoctoral Researcher with a strong experimental background. The successful candidate will develop quantitative experiments and imaging-based methods to characterize complex fracture behavior. Possible research directions include, but are not limited to, fracture of soft materials and architected materials, as well as dynamic crack propagation.

Job description

•
You will lead experimental research on the fracture mechanics of advanced materials, including architected materials and soft materials, using advanced imaging techniques, such as confocal imaging and high-speed imaging, to investigate complex fracture behavior near the crack tip

•
You will use image-based measurement techniques, such as digital image correlation (DIC), particle tracking, and other quantitative methods, to quantify displacement and strain fields, crack-tip deformation, fracture energy, and rate-dependent behavior

•
You will develop optical measurement methods to characterize interfacial contact, deformation, and friction in soft materials and architected materials

•
The position offers opportunities for close collaboration with researchers specializing in numerical modeling, theoretical analysis, and soft materials

•
In addition to carrying out independent research, the Postdoctoral Researcher will actively contribute to the supervision of junior researchers (e.g., PhD students and Master's students) within SMEC

• The position provides a stimulating environment for scientific growth and collaboration

Profile

• You have a doctoral degree in mechanics, (civil, mechanical, aerospace, or bio-) engineering, materials science, physics, or a related field

• You have hands-on experience in mechanical testing, experimental design, instrumentation, and quantitative measurements of material deformation and fracture

• Experience with digital image correlation, particle tracking, high-speed imaging, optical microscopy, or other quantitative optical measurement techniques is highly desirable

• You have the ability to independently develop and validate experimental methods, collaborate across disciplines, mentor students, and communicate effectively in English

• A commitment to open and reproducible research is expected

• You are curious, creative, and self-motivated, with a strong interest in understanding the physical mechanisms that govern material failure

• You enjoy working in an interdisciplinary environment an

descriptionByLocale.it:
Ricercatore post-dottorato: Meccanica di Frattura Sperimentale dei Materiali Morbidi

100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato

stampa
Druppo

Alla cattedra di Solid Mechanics (SMEC) dell'Istituto per i materiali da costruzione dell'ETH di Zurigo, ci proponiamo di capire come i materiali deformano, degradano, rompono e infine falliscono. La nostra ricerca è guidata dalla curiosità sui meccanismi fisici che sottomettono al fallimento e dall'ambizione di tradurre questa comprensione in materiali e strutture più affidabili e resilienti. Combinando la modellazione numerica, gli esperimenti di laboratorio e le analisi teoriche, cerchiamo di collegare i processi microscopici con il comportamento macroscopico dei sistemi ingegneristici e naturali e di sviluppare strumenti predittivi per il fallimento meccanico.

Il nostro team è altamente interdisciplinare e internazionale, che riunisce ricercatori con sfondi in scienza dei materiali, meccanica e fisica applicata. Lavoriamo attraverso una vasta gamma di argomenti, tra cui la meccanica dei sistemi di particelle (colloidale e granulare), materiali progettati e topologicamente interlocked, la meccanica della fragilità nel collagene, la meccanica dei terremoti, la frattura dei materiali morbidi e la modellazione del fallimento nei processi multifisici come la degradazione del cemento a corrosione. Ciò che unisce questi sforzi è una curiosità condivisa sul perché i materiali complessi falliscono e l'impegno a sviluppare nuovi concetti, esperimenti e modelli che avanzano la nostra comprensione della meccanica fallita.

Per espandere la nostra ricerca in meccanica di frattura sperimentale, stiamo cercando un ricercatore Postdoctoral motivato e innovativo con un forte background sperimentale. Il candidato di successo svilupperà esperimenti quantitativi e metodi basati sull'imaging per caratterizzare il comportamento di frattura complessa. Possibili direzioni di ricerca includono, ma non sono limitati a, frattura di materiali morbidi e materiali progettati, così come la propagazione dinamica della crepa.

Descrizione del lavoro

•
Condurrai ricerche sperimentali sulla meccanica delle fratture di materiali avanzati, inclusi materiali progettati e materiali morbidi, utilizzando tecniche di imaging avanzate, come l'imaging confocale e l'imaging ad alta velocità, per indagare il comportamento di frattura complessa vicino alla punta della crepa

•
Userete le tecniche di misura basate sull'immagine, come la correlazione dell'immagine digitale (DIC), il tracciamento delle particelle e altri metodi quantitativi, per quantificare i campi di spostamento e di deformazione, l'energia di frattura e il comportamento dipendente dai tassi

•
svilupperai metodi di misura ottica per caratterizzare il contatto interfacciale, la deformazione e l'attrito in materiali morbidi e materiali progettati

•
La posizione offre opportunità di stretta collaborazione con i ricercatori specializzati nella modellazione numerica, nell'analisi teorica e nei materiali morbidi

•
Oltre a svolgere ricerche indipendenti, il Ricercatore Postdoctoral contribuirà attivamente alla supervisione di ricercatori junior (ad esempio, studenti di dottorato e studenti di Master) all'interno di SMEC

• La posizione offre un ambiente stimolante per la crescita scientifica e la collaborazione

Profilo

• Hai una laurea in meccanica, (civile, meccanico, aerospaziale, o bio-) ingegneria, scienza dei materiali, fisica, o un campo correlato

• Hai esperienza pratica nel test meccanico, nella progettazione sperimentale, nella strumentazione e nelle misurazioni quantitative della deformazione e della frattura dei materiali

• L'esperienza con la correlazione delle immagini digitali, il tracciamento delle particelle, l'imaging ad alta velocità, la microscopia ottica, o altre tecniche di misurazione ottica quantitativa è altamente auspicabile

• Hai la capacità di sviluppare e convalidare in modo indipendente metodi sperimentali, collaborare in discipline, studenti mentori e comunicare efficacemente in inglese

• Si prevede un impegno per la ricerca aperta e riproducibile

• Siete curiosi, creativi e automotivati, con un forte interesse a comprendere i meccanismi fisici che governano il fallimento materiale

• Ti piace lavorare in un ambiente interdisciplinare
descriptionByLocale.en:
Postdoctoral Researcher: Experimental Fracture Mechanics of Soft Materials

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

At the Professorship of Solid Mechanics (SMEC) in the Institute for Building Materials at ETH Zurich, we aim to understand how materials deform, degrade, break, and ultimately fail. Our research is driven by curiosity about the physical mechanisms that underlie failure and by the ambition to translate this understanding into more reliable and resilient materials and structures. By combining numerical modeling, laboratory experiments, and theoretical analyses, we seek to link microscopic processes with the macroscopic behavior of both engineering and natural systems and develop predictive tools for mechanical failure.

Our team is highly interdisciplinary and international, bringing together researchers with backgrounds in materials science, mechanics, and applied physics. We work across a broad range of topics, including the mechanics of particle systems (colloidal and granular), architected and topologically interlocked materials, the mechanics of fragility in collagen, the mechanics of earthquakes, fracture of soft materials, and modeling failure in multiphysical processes such as corrosion-driven degradation of concrete. What unites these efforts is a shared curiosity about why complex materials fail and a commitment to developing new concepts, experiments, and models that advance our understanding of failure mechanics.

To expand our research in experimental fracture mechanics, we are seeking a motivated and innovative Postdoctoral Researcher with a strong experimental background. The successful candidate will develop quantitative experiments and imaging-based methods to characterize complex fracture behavior. Possible research directions include, but are not limited to, fracture of soft materials and architected materials, as well as dynamic crack propagation.

Job description

•
You will lead experimental research on the fracture mechanics of advanced materials, including architected materials and soft materials, using advanced imaging techniques, such as confocal imaging and high-speed imaging, to investigate complex fracture behavior near the crack tip

•
You will use image-based measurement techniques, such as digital image correlation (DIC), particle tracking, and other quantitative methods, to quantify displacement and strain fields, crack-tip deformation, fracture energy, and rate-dependent behavior

•
You will develop optical measurement methods to characterize interfacial contact, deformation, and friction in soft materials and architected materials

•
The position offers opportunities for close collaboration with researchers specializing in numerical modeling, theoretical analysis, and soft materials

•
In addition to carrying out independent research, the Postdoctoral Researcher will actively contribute to the supervision of junior researchers (e.g., PhD students and Master's students) within SMEC

• The position provides a stimulating environment for scientific growth and collaboration

Profile

• You have a doctoral degree in mechanics, (civil, mechanical, aerospace, or bio-) engineering, materials science, physics, or a related field

• You have hands-on experience in mechanical testing, experimental design, instrumentation, and quantitative measurements of material deformation and fracture

• Experience with digital image correlation, particle tracking, high-speed imaging, optical microscopy, or other quantitative optical measurement techniques is highly desirable

• You have the ability to independently develop and validate experimental methods, collaborate across disciplines, mentor students, and communicate effectively in English

• A commitment to open and reproducible research is expected

• You are curious, creative, and self-motivated, with a strong interest in understanding the physical mechanisms that govern material failure

• You enjoy working in an interdisciplinary environment an
descriptionByLocale.de:
Postdoktorand: Experimentelle Bruchmechanik weicher Materialien

100%, Zürich, befristet

Druck
Druckerzeugnisse

An der Professur für Festkörpermechanik (SMEC) am Institut für Baustoffe der ETH Zürich wollen wir verstehen, wie sich Materialien verformen, abbauen, brechen und letztlich versagen. Unsere Forschung basiert auf der Neugierde auf die physikalischen Mechanismen, die dem Versagen zugrunde liegen, und dem Ehrgeiz, dieses Verständnis in zuverlässigere und belastbarere Materialien und Strukturen umzusetzen. Durch die Kombination von numerischer Modellierung, Laborexperimenten und theoretischen Analysen wollen wir mikroskopische Prozesse mit dem makroskopischen Verhalten sowohl von technischen als auch von natürlichen Systemen verbinden und prädiktive Werkzeuge für mechanisches Versagen entwickeln.

Unser Team ist in hohem Maße interdisziplinär und international und bringt Forscher mit Hintergründen aus den Bereichen Materialwissenschaft, Mechanik und angewandte Physik zusammen. Wir arbeiten über ein breites Spektrum von Themen, einschließlich der Mechanik von Partikelsystemen (kolloidal und granular), architektonischen und topologisch ineinandergreifenden Materialien, der Mechanik der Fragilität in Kollagen, der Mechanik von Erdbeben, des Bruchs weicher Materialien und des Modellierungsversagens in multiphysikalischen Prozessen wie dem korrosionsbedingten Abbau von Beton. Was diese Bemühungen verbindet, ist die gemeinsame Neugierde, warum komplexe Materialien versagen, und die Verpflichtung, neue Konzepte, Experimente und Modelle zu entwickeln, die unser Verständnis der Fehlermechanik verbessern.

Um unsere Forschung in der experimentellen Frakturmechanik zu erweitern, suchen wir einen motivierten und innovativen Postdoktoranden mit einem starken experimentellen Hintergrund. Der erfolgreiche Kandidat wird quantitative Experimente und bildgebende Verfahren entwickeln, um komplexes Bruchverhalten zu charakterisieren. Mögliche Forschungsrichtungen umfassen, sind aber nicht beschränkt auf, Bruch von weichen Materialien und architektonischen Materialien, sowie dynamische Rissausbreitung.

Stellenbeschreibung

•
Sie werden experimentelle Forschung über die Bruchmechanik fortgeschrittener Materialien, einschließlich architektonischer Materialien und weicher Materialien, mit fortschrittlichen Bildgebungstechniken wie konfokaler Bildgebung und Hochgeschwindigkeitsbildgebung leiten, um komplexes Bruchverhalten in der Nähe der Rissspitze zu untersuchen

•
Sie werden bildbasierte Messtechniken wie digitale Bildkorrelation (DIC), Partikelverfolgung und andere quantitative Methoden verwenden, um Verschiebungs- und Dehnungsfelder, Rissspitzendeformation, Bruchenergie und ratenabhängiges Verhalten zu quantifizieren

•
Sie entwickeln optische Messmethoden zur Charakterisierung von Grenzflächenkontakt, Verformung und Reibung in weichen Materialien und architektonischen Materialien

•
Die Position bietet Möglichkeiten für eine enge Zusammenarbeit mit Forschern, die sich auf numerische Modellierung, theoretische Analyse und weiche Materialien spezialisiert haben.

•
Neben der unabhängigen Forschung wird der Postdoktorand aktiv zur Betreuung von Nachwuchsforschern (z.B. Doktoranden und Masterstudenten) innerhalb der SMEC beitragen.

• Die Position bietet ein stimulierendes Umfeld für wissenschaftliche Wachstum und Zusammenarbeit

Profil

• Sie haben einen Doktorgrad in Mechanik, (Zivil-, Mechanik-, Luft- und Raumfahrt- oder Bio-) Ingenieurwesen, Materialwissenschaften, Physik oder einem verwandten Bereich

• Sie haben praktische Erfahrung in mechanischen Tests, experimentellem Design, Instrumentierung und quantitativen Messungen von Materialverformung und Bruch

• Erfahrung mit digitaler Bildkorrelation, Partikelverfolgung, Hochgeschwindigkeitsbildgebung, optischer Mikroskopie oder anderen quantitativen optischen Messtechniken ist sehr wünschenswert

• Sie haben die Möglichkeit, experimentelle Methoden unabhängig zu entwickeln und zu validieren, disziplinübergreifend zusammenzuarbeiten, Studenten zu betreuen und effektiv auf Englisch zu kommunizieren.

• Ein Engagement für offene und reproduzierbare Forschung wird erwartet

• Sie sind neugierig, kreativ und selbstmotiviert, mit einem starken Interesse daran, die physikalischen Mechanismen zu verstehen, die das materielle Versagen steuern

• Sie arbeiten gerne in einem interdisziplinären Umfeld und
descriptionByLocale.fr:
Chercheur postdoctoral : Mécanique expérimentale de la fracture des matériaux souples

100%, Zurich, durée déterminée

imprimer
Drucken

Au Professeur de Mécanique Solide (SMEC) à l'Institut des matériaux de construction à l'ETH Zurich, nous voulons comprendre comment les matériaux déforment, dégradent, brisent et finalement échouent. Nos recherches sont motivées par la curiosité au sujet des mécanismes physiques qui sous-tendent l'échec et par l'ambition de traduire cette compréhension en matériaux et structures plus fiables et plus résistants. En combinant la modélisation numérique, les expériences de laboratoire et les analyses théoriques, nous cherchons à lier les processus microscopiques au comportement macroscopique des systèmes d'ingénierie et des systèmes naturels et à développer des outils prédictifs pour la défaillance mécanique.

Notre équipe est hautement interdisciplinaire et internationale, réunissant des chercheurs ayant des connaissances en sciences des matériaux, en mécanique et en physique appliquée. Nous travaillons sur un large éventail de sujets, y compris la mécanique des systèmes de particules (colloïdaux et granulaires), les matériaux architecturés et topologiques entrelacés, la mécanique de la fragilité du collagène, la mécanique des tremblements de terre, la fracture des matériaux mous et l'échec de la modélisation dans des processus multiphysiques tels que la dégradation du béton par la corrosion. Ce qui unit ces efforts est une curiosité commune sur la raison pour laquelle les matériaux complexes échouent et un engagement à développer de nouveaux concepts, des expériences et des modèles qui font progresser notre compréhension de la mécanique de défaillance.

Pour élargir notre recherche en mécanique expérimentale des fractures, nous recherchons un chercheur postdoctoral motivé et innovateur ayant une solide expérience. Le candidat retenu développera des expériences quantitatives et des méthodes basées sur l'imagerie pour caractériser un comportement de fracture complexe. Les directions de recherche possibles comprennent, sans s'y limiter, la fracture des matériaux mous et des matériaux d'architecture, ainsi que la propagation dynamique des fissures.

Description du poste

•
Vous dirigerez des recherches expérimentales sur la mécanique de fracture des matériaux avancés, y compris les matériaux d'architecture et les matériaux mous, en utilisant des techniques d'imagerie avancées, telles que l'imagerie confocale et l'imagerie à grande vitesse, pour étudier le comportement de fracture complexe près de l'extrémité de la fissure

•
Vous utiliserez des techniques de mesure basées sur l'image, telles que la corrélation numérique d'image (DIC), le suivi des particules et d'autres méthodes quantitatives, pour quantifier les champs de déplacement et de déformation, la déformation du crack-tip, l'énergie de fracture et le comportement dépendant de la vitesse

•
Vous développerez des méthodes de mesure optique pour caractériser le contact interfacial, la déformation et le frottement dans les matériaux mous et les matériaux d'architecture

•
Le poste offre des possibilités de collaboration étroite avec des chercheurs spécialisés dans la modélisation numérique, l'analyse théorique et les matériaux souples

•
En plus d'effectuer des recherches indépendantes, le chercheur postdoctoral contribuera activement à la supervision des chercheurs subalternes (p. ex., les doctorants et les étudiants à la maîtrise) au sein du CMPE.

• La position offre un environnement stimulant pour la croissance scientifique et la collaboration

Profil

• Vous avez un doctorat en mécanique, (civil, mécanique, aérospatiale ou bio-) génie, sciences des matériaux, physique ou un domaine connexe

• Vous avez une expérience pratique dans les essais mécaniques, la conception expérimentale, l'instrumentation et les mesures quantitatives de la déformation et de la fracture du matériau

• L'expérience de la corrélation numérique, du suivi des particules, de l'imagerie à grande vitesse, de la microscopie optique ou d'autres techniques quantitatives de mesure optique est hautement souhaitable.

• Vous avez la capacité de développer et de valider des méthodes expérimentales indépendantes, de collaborer entre disciplines, de guider les étudiants et de communiquer efficacement en anglais

• Un engagement à la recherche ouverte et reproductible est attendu

• Vous êtes curieux, créatif et automotivé, avec un vif intérêt à comprendre les mécanismes physiques qui gouvernent l'échec matériel

• Vous aimez travailler dans un environnement interdisciplinaire

jobs.description:
ETH AI Center Post-Doc Fellowship 2027

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The ETH AI Center promotes trustworthy, accessible, and inclusive AI systems. For this goal, we bring together interdisciplinary research teams of AI foundations, applications, and implications across all departments and look at AI from many different angles like mathematical principles, medicine, architecture, robotics, and social sciences / future of work. We enable research of high quality, industry innovation, and AI entrepreneurship.

Project background

The ETH AI Center faculty comprises more than 140 professorships representing all sixteen departments of ETH Zurich and external research groups from University of Zurich and University of St.Gallen. The ETH AI Center Fellowship program is Europe’s premier Post-Doc program focused on advancing interdisciplinary AI research. This can be inside AI foundations or between AI foundations and application areas. As a truly interdisciplinary program, fellows work with two excellent PIs who are from different fields and carry equal weights in the supervision.

Job description

Within the post-doctoral fellowship program, you will conduct research that impacts the future of AI. You will be working on your project (that you will propose) and continuously have the opportunity to exchange with other teams and professorships, and participate at faculty retreats, symposia, summits, etc. Fellows have their primary office at the ETH AI Center and enjoy excellent employment conditions. The center offers plenty of opportunities to strengthen your career path through an optional entrepreneurial or industry track that provides you with valuable hands-on experience to turn your research into practical impact.

Profile

• You either already hold a PhD or will complete your doctorate at least 3 months before the beginning of the fellowship program (latest by June 2027)

• You have a background in relevant AI fields or in one of the following: computer science, physics, engineering, applied mathematics

• Your level of English allows you to discuss your topics with your colleagues and report your Findings in writing

• You look forward to working with an interdisciplinary team that longs to find solutions together

Workplace

We offer

We offer 8 - 12 post-doctoral positions and the occupation normally runs for two years. Starting date is flexible but typically in September 2027. A post-doc is experienced by many as a great stepping stone into R&D lab leadership in industry, a start-up or a faculty position. It is a valuable time to sharpen your profile.

• Co-mentorship by two excellent PIs of different fields

• Training and continuing education activities and language courses are available at an affordable price

• 5 weeks vacation/year

• ETH Zurich offers subsidies for childcare

• Eight dedicated daycare centers for kids close to the campus

• 4 months paid maternity leave/10 days paid paternity leave

• Up to 5 days paid leave for care of sick in own household

• Up to 5 days paid leave for educators for school matters

• Medical clarifications with children

Curious? So are we.

Further information about ETH AI Center can be found on our website .
Before applying, please read carefully our guidelines: ETH AI Center Post-Doc Fellowship Guidelines and visit our FAQs . The deadline for applications is October 27, 2026 (16:00 CET). Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

ETH AI Center Fellowship post-doc 2027

100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato

stampa Drucken

Il Centro ETH AI promuove sistemi AI affidabili, accessibili e inclusivi. Consentiamo la ricerca di alta qualità, innovazione industriale e imprenditorialità.

Contesto del progetto

La facoltà di ETH AI Center comprende oltre 140 cattedrali che rappresentano tutti i sedici dipartimenti di ETH Zurigo e gruppi di ricerca esterni dell'Università di Zurigo e dell'Università di St.Gallen. Il programma di Fellowship di ETH AI Center è Europe.s.s. kicker Post-Doc, che si concentra sull'avanzamento della ricerca interdisciplinare AI. Può essere all'interno di basi AI o tra fondazioni e aree applicative.

Descrizione del lavoro

All'interno del programma di borse post-dottorale, condurrà la ricerca che ha impatto sul futuro di AI. Lavorerà sul vostro progetto (che proporrete) e avrà l'opportunità di scambiare continuamente con altre squadre e professori, e partecipare a ritiri di facoltà, simposi, vertici, ecc. I signori hanno il loro ufficio primario presso il centro ETH AI e godono di eccellenti condizioni di lavoro.

Il centro offre molte opportunità per rafforzare il percorso di carriera attraverso un percorso imprenditoriale opzionale o industriale che fornisce una preziosa esperienza pratica per trasformare la vostra ricerca in impatto pratico.

Profilo

• O è già in possesso di un dottorato o completerà il dottorato almeno 3 mesi prima dell'inizio del programma di borse di studio (ultima entro giugno 2027)

• Hai un background in campi pertinenti di AI o in uno dei seguenti: informatica, fisica, ingegneria, matematica applicata

• Il tuo livello di inglese ti permette di discutere i tuoi argomenti con i tuoi colleghi e di riferire i tuoi risultati per iscritto

• Non vedi l'ora di lavorare con un team interdisciplinare che anela alla ricerca di soluzioni insieme

Posto di lavoro

Offriamo

Offriamo 8 - 12 posizioni post-dottorale e l'occupazione normalmente funziona per due anni. La data di inizio è flessibile ma tipicamente nel settembre 2027. Un post-dottorato è sperimentato da molti come una grande pietra miliare nella leadership di laboratorio R&D nel settore, una start-up o una posizione di facoltà. È un momento prezioso per affinare il vostro profilo.

• Co-mento da parte di due eccellenti PI di diversi campi

• Attività di formazione e formazione continua e corsi di lingua sono disponibili ad un prezzo accessibile

5 settimane di vacation/year

• ETH Zurigo offre sussidi per l'infanzia

• Otto centri di asilo nido dedicati ai bambini vicino al campus

• 4 mesi di congedo di maternità retribuito/10 giorni di congedo di paternità retribuito

• Fino a 5 giorni di congedo retribuito per la cura degli ammalati in casa propria

• Fino a 5 giorni di congedo retribuito per gli educatori per le questioni scolastiche

• Delucidazioni mediche con i bambini

Anche noi.

Per ulteriori informazioni su ETH AI Center, consultare le nostre linee guida: ETH AI Center Linee guida post-Doc e visitare le nostre FAQ. La scadenza per le domande è il 27 ottobre, 2026 (16:00 CET). Si prega di notare che accettiamo esclusivamente le domande presentate attraverso il nostro portale di applicazione online. Le domande tramite e-mail o servizi postali non saranno prese in considerazione.

ETH AI Center Post-Doc Fellowship 2027

100%, Zürich, befristet

Druckdruck

Das ETH AI Center fördert vertrauenswürdige, zugängliche und inklusive KI-Systeme. Dazu bringen wir interdisziplinäre Forschungsteams von KI-Stiftungen, Anwendungen und Implikationen in allen Abteilungen zusammen und betrachten KI aus vielen verschiedenen Blickwinkeln wie mathematische Prinzipien, Medizin, Architektur, Robotik und Sozialwissenschaften/Zukunft der Arbeit. Wir ermöglichen Forschung von hoher Qualität, Industrieinnovation und KI-Unternehmertum.

Projekthintergrund

Die Fakultät des ETH AI Centers umfasst mehr als 140 Professuren für alle sechzehn Departements der ETH Zürich und externe Forschungsgruppen der Universität Zürich und der Universität St.Gallen. Das ETH AI Center Fellowship Programm ist Europa, das führende Post-Doc-Programm, das sich auf die Förderung interdisziplinärer KI-Forschung konzentriert. Dies kann innerhalb von KI-Stiftungen oder zwischen KI-Stiftungen und Anwendungsbereichen liegen. Stipendiaten arbeiten als wirklich interdisziplinäres Programm mit zwei exzellenten PIs, die aus verschiedenen Bereichen stammen und in der Betreuung gleichgewichtig sind.

Arbeitsplatzbeschreibung

Im Rahmen des Post-doctoral-Stipendiums werden Sie forschen, was die Zukunft der KI beeinflusst. Sie arbeiten an Ihrem Projekt (das Sie vorschlagen) und haben kontinuierlich die Möglichkeit, sich mit anderen Teams und Professuren auszutauschen, an Fakultätsreferenten, Symposien, Gipfeln etc. teilzunehmen. Fellows haben ihr erstes Büro am ETH KI-Zentrum und genießen hervorragende Arbeitsbedingungen.

Das Zentrum bietet Ihnen viele Möglichkeiten, Ihren Karriereweg durch einen optionalen unternehmerischen oder branchenspezifischen Track zu stärken, der Ihnen wertvolle praktische Erfahrungen bietet, um Ihre Forschung in praktische Wirkung zu verwandeln.

Profil

• Sie haben bereits einen Doktortitel oder werden mindestens 3 Monate vor Beginn des Stipendienprogramms promoviert (Ende Juni 2027)

• Sie haben einen Hintergrund in relevanten KI-Bereichen oder in einem der folgenden: Informatik, Physik, Ingenieurwesen, angewandte Mathematik

• Ihr Englischniveau ermöglicht es Ihnen, Ihre Themen mit Ihren Kollegen zu besprechen und Ihre Ergebnisse schriftlich zu melden

• Sie freuen sich auf die Zusammenarbeit mit einem interdisziplinären Team, das sich nach Lösungen sehnt

Arbeitsplatz

Wir bieten

Wir bieten 8 - 12 Post-doc-Stellen an und die Besetzung dauert normalerweise zwei Jahre. Beginn ist flexibel, aber typischerweise im September 2027. Ein Post-doc wird von vielen als großer Schritt in die F&E-Laborleitung in der Industrie, ein Start-up oder eine Fakultätsposition erlebt. Es ist eine wertvolle Zeit, Ihr Profil zu schärfen.

• Co-Mentorship durch zwei ausgezeichnete PIs aus verschiedenen Bereichen

jobs.description:
ETH AI Center Doctoral Fellowship 2027

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The ETH AI Center promotes trustworthy, accessible, and inclusive AI systems. For this goal, we bring together interdisciplinary research teams of AI foundations, applications, and implications across all departments and look at AI from many different angles like mathematical principles, medicine, architecture, robotics, and social sciences / future of work. We enable research of high quality, industry innovation, and AI entrepreneurship.

Project background

The ETH AI Center faculty comprises more than 140 professorships representing all sixteen departments of ETH Zurich and external research groups from University of Zurich and University of St.Gallen. The ETH AI Center Fellowship program is Europe’s premier PhD program focused on advancing interdisciplinary AI research. This can be inside AI foundations or between AI foundations and application areas. As a truly interdisciplinary program, fellows work with two excellent PIs who are from different fields and carry equal weights in the supervision.

Job description

Within the doctoral fellowship program you will conduct research that impacts the future of AI. You will be working on your own project (that you will propose) and continuously have the opportunity to exchange with other teams and professorships, participate at faculty retreats, symposia, summits etc. Fellows have their primary office at the ETH AI Center and enjoy excellent employment conditions. The center offers plenty of opportunities to strengthen your career path through an optional entrepreneurial or industry track that provides you with valuable hands-on experience to turn your research into practical impact.

Profile

• You are expected to have completed or will complete a Master’s degree in computer science, machine learning, statistics, physics, engineering, applied mathematics, or other relevant fields, at least 3 months before the beginning of the fellowship program (latest by June 2027)

• You have an excellent track record and must meet the general admission requirements for a doctorate at ETH Zurich (available here )

• Your level of English allows you to discuss your topics with your colleagues and report your findings in writing

• You look forward to working with an interdisciplinary team that longs to find solutions together

Workplace

We offer

We offer around 8 - 12 doctoral positions and the occupation normally runs for three years. For Fellows with good progress, it can be extended for a maximum of one year to complete the doctoral thesis (decision to be taken by the ETH AI Center Doctoral Selection Committee, without additional interviews). Starting date is flexible but typically in September 2027.

• Co-mentorship by two excellent PIs of different fields

• Training and continuing education activities and language courses at an affordable price

• Services and offerings to support work and family life

Curious? So are we.

Further information about ETH AI Center can be found on our website .
Before applying, please read carefully our guidelines: ETH AI Center Doctoral Fellowship Guidelines and visit our FAQs . The deadline for applications is October 27, 2026 (16:00 CET). Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

descriptionByLocale.it:
ETH AI Centro Fleoship Dottorale 2027

100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato

stampa Drucken

Il Centro ETH AI promuove sistemi AI affidabili, accessibili e inclusivi. A tal fine, riuniamo gruppi di ricerca interdisciplinare di fondazioni, applicazioni e implicazioni in tutti i reparti e guardiamo l'AI da molte angolazioni diverse come principi matematici, medicina, architettura, robotica e scienze sociali / futuro del lavoro. Consentiamo la ricerca di alta qualità, innovazione industriale e imprenditorialità.

Contesto del progetto

La facoltà di ETH AI Center comprende oltre 140 cattedrali che rappresentano tutti i sedici dipartimenti di ETH Zurigo e gruppi di ricerca esterni dell'Università di Zurigo e dell'Università di St.Gallen. Il programma di Fellowship di ETH AI Center è il programma di dottorato in Europa. Il programma di ricerca interdisciplinare si concentra sull'avanzamento della ricerca interdisciplinare AI. Può essere all'interno di fondazioni AI o tra fondazioni e aree applicative.

Descrizione del lavoro

All'interno del programma di dottorato si condurrà la ricerca che ha impatto sul futuro di AI. Lavorerete sul vostro progetto (che si proporrà) e avranno la possibilità di scambiare con altre squadre e professori, partecipare a ritiri di facoltà, simposi, vertici ecc. I compagni hanno il loro ufficio primario presso il centro ETH AI e godere di eccellenti condizioni di lavoro.

Il centro offre molte opportunità per rafforzare il percorso di carriera attraverso un percorso imprenditoriale opzionale o industriale che fornisce una preziosa esperienza pratica per trasformare la vostra ricerca in impatto pratico.

Profilo

• Si prevede di aver completato o completerà un Master.s in informatica, machine learning, statistica, fisica, ingegneria, matematica applicata, o altri campi pertinenti, almeno 3 mesi prima dell'inizio del programma di borse di studio (ultimo entro giugno 2027)

• Hai un ottimo curriculum e devi soddisfare i requisiti generali di ammissione per un dottorato presso ETH Zurigo (disponibile qui)

• Il tuo livello di inglese ti permette di discutere i tuoi argomenti con i tuoi colleghi e di riferire i tuoi risultati per iscritto

• Non vedi l'ora di lavorare con un team interdisciplinare che anela alla ricerca di soluzioni insieme

Posto di lavoro

Offriamo

Per i Fellows con buoni progressi, può essere esteso per un massimo di un anno per completare la tesi di dottorato (decisione che deve essere presa dal Comitato di Selezione del Dottorato ETH AI Center, senza ulteriori interviste). La data di inizio è flessibile ma tipicamente nel settembre 2027.

• Co-mento da parte di due eccellenti PI di diversi campi

• Attività di formazione e formazione continua e corsi di lingua a prezzi accessibili

• Servizi e offerte per il sostegno alla vita professionale e familiare

Anche noi.

Ulteriori informazioni su ETH AI Center sono disponibili sul nostro sito web. Prima di applicare, si prega di leggere attentamente le nostre linee guida: ETH AI Center Dottorato linee guida e visitare le nostre FAQ. La scadenza per le domande è ottobre 27, 2026 (16:00 CET). Si prega di notare che accettiamo esclusivamente le domande presentate attraverso il nostro portale di applicazione online. Le applicazioni via e-mail o servizi postali non saranno prese in considerazione.

descriptionByLocale.de:
ETH AI Center Doktorandenstipendium 2027

100%, Zürich, befristet

Druckdruck

Das ETH AI Center fördert vertrauenswürdige, zugängliche und inklusive KI-Systeme. Dazu bringen wir interdisziplinäre Forschungsteams von KI-Stiftungen, Anwendungen und Implikationen in allen Abteilungen zusammen und betrachten KI aus vielen verschiedenen Blickwinkeln wie mathematische Prinzipien, Medizin, Architektur, Robotik und Sozialwissenschaften/Zukunft der Arbeit. Wir ermöglichen Forschung von hoher Qualität, Industrieinnovation und KI-Unternehmertum.

Projekthintergrund

Die Fakultät des ETH AI Center umfasst mehr als 140 Professuren, die alle sechzehn Departements der ETH Zürich und externe Forschungsgruppen der Universität Zürich und der Universität St.Gallen vertreten. Das ETH AI Center Fellowship Programm ist Europa, das führende Doktorandenprogramm, das sich auf die Förderung interdisziplinärer KI-Forschung konzentriert. Dies kann innerhalb von KI-Stiftungen oder zwischen KI-Stiftungen und Anwendungsbereichen liegen. Als wirklich interdisziplinäres Programm arbeiten Stipendiaten mit zwei exzellenten PIs, die aus verschiedenen Bereichen stammen und in der Betreuung gleiche Gewichte tragen.

Arbeitsplatzbeschreibung

Im Rahmen des Promotionsstipendiums forschen Sie, was die Zukunft der KI beeinflusst. Sie arbeiten an Ihrem eigenen Projekt (das Sie vorschlagen) und haben die Möglichkeit, sich mit anderen Teams und Professuren auszutauschen, an Fakultätsretreats, Symposien, Gipfeln etc. teilzunehmen. Fellows haben ihr erstes Büro am ETH AI Center und genießen hervorragende Arbeitsbedingungen.

Das Zentrum bietet Ihnen viele Möglichkeiten, Ihren Karriereweg durch einen optionalen unternehmerischen oder branchenspezifischen Track zu stärken, der Ihnen wertvolle praktische Erfahrungen bietet, um Ihre Forschung in praktische Wirkung zu verwandeln.

Profil

• Sie werden voraussichtlich mindestens 3 Monate vor Beginn des Stipendienprogramms einen Master in Informatik, Maschinenbau, Statistik, Physik, Ingenieurwesen, angewandter Mathematik oder anderen relevanten Bereichen abgeschlossen haben oder diesen Abschluss abschließen (spätestens bis Juni 2027)

• Sie haben eine hervorragende Erfolgsbilanz und müssen die allgemeinen Zulassungsvoraussetzungen für eine Promotion an der ETH Zürich erfüllen (hier erhältlich )

• Ihr Englischniveau ermöglicht es Ihnen, Ihre Themen mit Ihren Kollegen zu besprechen und Ihre Ergebnisse schriftlich zu melden

• Sie freuen sich auf die Zusammenarbeit mit einem interdisziplinären Team, das sich nach Lösungen sehnt

Arbeitsplatz

Wir bieten

Wir bieten rund 8 - 12 Doktoratspositionen an und die Besetzung dauert in der Regel drei Jahre. Für Stipendiaten mit gutem Fortschritt kann sie um maximal ein Jahr auf den Abschluss der Doktorarbeit verlängert werden (Entscheidung des Promotionsauswahlausschusses des ETH-AI-Zentrums, ohne zusätzliche Interviews).

• Co-Mentorship durch zwei ausgezeichnete PIs aus verschiedenen Bereichen

• Weiterbildungs- und Sprachkurse zu einem erschwinglichen Preis

• Dienstleistungen und Angebote zur Unterstützung von Beruf und Familie

- Neugierig?

Weitere Informationen zum ETH AI Center finden Sie auf unserer Website. Bitte lesen Sie vor der Bewerbung unsere Richtlinien: ETH AI Center Doctoral Fellowship Guidelines und besuchen Sie unsere FAQs. Bewerbungsfrist ist der 27. Oktober 2026 (16:00 CET). Bitte beachten Sie, dass wir ausschließlich über unser Online-Bewerbungsportal eingereichte Bewerbungen akzeptieren. Bewerbungen per E-Mail oder Post werden nicht berücksichtigt.

jobs.description:
Doctoral Student in Design and Analysis of Human-AI Systems

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Decision Sciences and Analytics group, led by Prof. Tu Ni at ETH Zürich is seeking a doctoral student to study the design and analysis of human-AI systems. This position focuses on the development of AI systems with an emphasis on understanding and reshaping the role of human. The study context is broad, such as AI for clinical or legal decisions, AI for learning and education, etc. The research is mainly theoretical, but will be related to empirical study like field/lab experiments when necessary.

Job description

• Analyze AI systems where the decision is often high-stake or with long-term impact

• Design AI systems that lead to efficient and reliable outcomes

• Write high-quality papers and publish on top-tier OM journals

• Work with external organizations to evaluate the methods if needed

• In addition to research activities, they will contribute to lab responsibilities (e.g. teaching, advising master thesis)

Profile

• Hold (or will have completed at the time of appointment) a Master’s degree in applied mathematics, economics, operations, or a closely related field

• Excellent academic records and is motivated to produce high-quality, policy-relevant research

• Have excellent analytical and modeling skills: optimization, mechanism design, etc

• Have excellent verbal and written communication skills

• Have industrial experience in AI deployment is a plus

Workplace

We offer

• The starting date is negotiable, but hopefully in six months

• The position is initially offered for 18 months, with the prospect of extension for four- to five-year duration of the doctorate, subject to satisfactory progress

• We offer the opportunity to pursue a high-quality PhD at a renowned institution and to work in a dynamic and collaborative research environment

• Gross salary will be in accordance with the regulatons of ETH Zurich

chevron_right
Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich

We value diversity and sustainability

In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .

Curious? So are we.

We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents :

• A letter of motivation that includes an explanation why you are interested in doing a PhD and fit for the position (within one page)

• A resume/CV

• Complete academic record with undergraduate and graduate courses and grades

• Arrange at least two references and provide the contact information

Further information about our Department can be found on our Website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Tu Ni, tunitu@ethz.ch (no applications or unsolicited outreach).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

About ETH Zürich

ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.

100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato

stampa
Druppo

Il gruppo Decision Sciences and Analytics, guidato dal Prof. Tu Ni a ETH Zürich sta cercando uno studente di dottorato per studiare la progettazione e l'analisi dei sistemi umani-AI. Questa posizione si concentra sullo sviluppo dei sistemi AI con l'accento sulla comprensione e sulla rimodellazione del ruolo dell'uomo. Il contesto di studio è ampio, come l'IA per le decisioni cliniche o legali, l'IA per l'apprendimento e l'istruzione, ecc. La ricerca è principalmente teorica, ma sarà legata allo studio empirico come esperimenti sul campo/lastra quando necessario.

Descrizione del lavoro

• Analizzare i sistemi AI in cui la decisione è spesso ad alto consumo o con impatto a lungo termine

• Sistemi di progettazione AI che portano a risultati efficienti e affidabili

• Scrivere documenti di alta qualità e pubblicare su riviste OM top-tier

• Lavorare con organizzazioni esterne per valutare i metodi se necessario

• Oltre alle attività di ricerca, contribuiranno a responsabilità di laboratorio (ad es. l'insegnamento, la consulenza di tesi master)

Profilo

• Hold (o avrà completato al momento della nomina) un Master in matematica applicata, economia, operazioni, o un campo strettamente correlato

• Ottimi documenti accademici ed è motivato a produrre ricerca di alta qualità, politica-rilevante

• Avere eccellenti capacità analitiche e di modellazione: ottimizzazione, progettazione di meccanismi, ecc

• Avere eccellenti capacità di comunicazione verbale e scritta

• Avere esperienza industriale nella distribuzione AI è un vantaggio

Luogo di lavoro

Offriamo

• La data di partenza è negoziabile, ma speriamo in sei mesi

• La posizione è inizialmente offerta per 18 mesi, con la prospettiva di proroga per la durata di quattro o cinque anni del dottorato, con un progresso soddisfacente

• Offriamo l'opportunità di perseguire un dottorato di alta qualità in una rinomata istituzione e di lavorare in un ambiente di ricerca dinamico e collaborativo

• Lo stipendio lordo sarà conforme ai regolamenti dell'ETH di Zurigo

Apprezziamo la diversità e la sostenibilità

Doctoral Student in Design and Analysis of Human-AI Systems

100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

The Decision Sciences and Analytics group, led by Prof. Tu Ni at ETH Zürich is seeking a doctoral student to study the design and analysis of human-AI systems. This position focuses on the development of AI systems with an emphasis on understanding and reshaping the role of human. The study context is broad, such as AI for clinical or legal decisions, AI for learning and education, etc. The research is mainly theoretical, but will be related to empirical study like field/lab experiments when necessary.

Job description

• Analyze AI systems where the decision is often high-stake or with long-term impact

• Design AI systems that lead to efficient and reliable outcomes

• Write high-quality papers and publish on top-tier OM journals

• Work with external organizations to evaluate the methods if needed

• In addition to research activities, they will contribute to lab responsibilities (e.g. teaching, advising master thesis)

Profile

• Hold (or will have completed at the time of appointment) a Master’s degree in applied mathematics, economics, operations, or a closely related field

• Excellent academic records and is motivated to produce high-quality, policy-relevant research

• Have excellent analytical and modeling skills: optimization, mechanism design, etc

• Have excellent verbal and written communication skills

• Have industrial experience in AI deployment is a plus

Workplace

We offer

• The starting date is negotiable, but hopefully in six months

• The position is initially offered for 18 months, with the prospect of extension for four- to five-year duration of the doctorate, subject to satisfactory progress

jobs.description:
Flight Software Systems Engineer for Space Missions

80%-100%, Zurich, fixed-term

print
Drucken

Led by Prof. Dr. Thomas Zurbuchen, ETH Zurich | Space brings together space-related research, education and technology development across ETH Zurich. Working with academic, industrial and institutional partners, the initiative develops new space missions, instruments and technologies.

This position is offered as a fixed-term appointment for an initial period of two years, with the possibility of extension.

Project background

The objective of this initiative is to establish and grow a centralized pool of space engineering expertise within ETH Zurich | Space. This pool supports ETH Zurich-led space projects and technology programs, strengthening ETH Zurich’s role in the Swiss and international space ecosystem.

The Flight Software Systems Engineer will support a diverse portfolio of small spacecraft, scientific instruments, robotic systems, and technology demonstrators. The work includes resource-constrained missions, integration with externally supplied spacecraft platforms, autonomous functions, and future distributed or coordinated spacecraft concepts. This role interfaces across systems engineering, avionics, payloads, and software development, and coordinates with external platform providers and mission operations teams.

Job description

As part of the specialized resource pool, you will provide flight software and software systems engineering expertise across multiple ETH Zurich space projects. You will contribute from early mission formulation and software architecture through implementation, integration, verification, launch preparation, and operations.

As part of your role, you will:

• Take technical ownership of assigned flight software developments and act as the primary software interface to systems engineering, avionics, payload teams, mission operations, and external platform providers.

• Translate mission concept of operations into spacecraft behaviors and define flight software architectures and functional decompositions

• Allocate hardware-software functions, and define associated software requirements and interfaces.

• Translate mission and system requirements into software specifications, interface control documents, operational concepts, and verification plans.

• Develop embedded flight software in C and C++ and supporting tools and test scripts (e.g., Python), including device drivers, telemetry and telecommand handling, onboard data management, application software, and fault-management functions.

• Integrate flight software with onboard computers, sensors, actuators, payload electronics, communication interfaces, ground systems, and externally supplied spacecraft platforms.

• Set up and maintain flat-sat flight software testbeds

• Perform software-related trade studies covering processing capacity, memory, timing, bandwidth, autonomy, reliability, and fault tolerance.

• Develop real-time, event-driven, autonomous, synchronization, and GNC-related software functions where required.

• Establish and maintain software baselines, configuration control, versioning, build automation, continuous integration, release management, and requirements traceability.

• Develop and execute flight software unit tests, conduct integration, software-in-the-loop, processor-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop, and system-level verification and validation activities.

• Support software risk management, anomaly investigation, non-conformance handling, and technical review boards.

• Support spacecraft and payload assembly, integration, and test activities, commissioning, in-flight software updates, telemetry analysis, and mission operations.

• Contribute to technical reviews, early-stage mission concepts, proposals, and software feasibility studies.

• Provide technical guidance to junior engineers, researchers, and student teams.

Profile

You have a strong background in embedded and real-time software developme

descriptionByLocale.it:
Ingegnere di sistemi di volo per missioni spaziali

80%-100%, Zurigo, a tempo determinato

stampa
Druppo

Guidato dal Prof. Dr. Thomas Zurbuchen, ETH Zurich | Space riunisce la ricerca spaziale, l'istruzione e lo sviluppo tecnologico in tutta l'ETH di Zurigo. Lavorando con partner accademici, industriali e istituzionali, l'iniziativa sviluppa nuove missioni spaziali, strumenti e tecnologie.

Questa posizione è offerta come appuntamento fisso per un periodo iniziale di due anni, con la possibilità di prolungamento.

Sfondo del progetto

L'obiettivo di questa iniziativa è quello di stabilire e crescere un pool centralizzato di competenze di ingegneria spaziale all'interno di ETH Zurich | Space. Questa piscina supporta progetti spaziali e programmi tecnologici guidati dall’ETH di Zurigo, rafforzando il ruolo di ETH Zurigo nell’ecosistema spaziale svizzero e internazionale.

L'Ingegnere di Sistemi di Volo sosterrà un portafoglio diversificato di piccoli veicoli spaziali, strumenti scientifici, sistemi robotizzati e dimostranti tecnologici. Il lavoro comprende missioni contratta di risorse, integrazione con piattaforme di veicoli spaziali esternamente fornite, funzioni autonome e futuri concetti di veicoli spaziali distribuiti o coordinati. Questo ruolo si interfaccia tra sistemi di ingegneria, avionica, payload e sviluppo software, e coordina con fornitori di piattaforme esterne e team di operazioni di missione.

Descrizione del lavoro

Nell'ambito del pool di risorse specializzato, fornirete competenze di ingegneria software e software di volo in più progetti spaziali ETH Zurigo. Contribuirai dalla formulazione iniziale della missione e dall'architettura del software attraverso l'implementazione, l'integrazione, la verifica, la preparazione del lancio e le operazioni.

Come parte del vostro ruolo, voi:

• Assumere la proprietà tecnica degli sviluppi del software di volo assegnati e agire come l'interfaccia software principale per l'ingegneria dei sistemi, avionica, team di carico, operazioni di missione e fornitori di piattaforme esterne.

• Tradurre il concetto di missione di operazioni in comportamenti di veicolo spaziale e definire architetture di software di volo e decomposizioni funzionali

• Allocare le funzioni hardware-software e definire i requisiti e le interfacce software associati.

• Traduci i requisiti di missione e di sistema nelle specifiche del software, documenti di controllo dell'interfaccia, concetti operativi e piani di verifica.

• Sviluppare software di volo incorporato in C e C++ e strumenti di supporto e script di test (ad esempio, Python), inclusi driver di dispositivo, gestione della telemetria e del telecomand, gestione dei dati di bordo, software di applicazione e funzioni di gestione dei guasti.

• Integra software di volo con computer a bordo, sensori, attuatori, elettronica di carico, interfacce di comunicazione, sistemi di terra e piattaforme di veicoli spaziali esternamente fornite.

• Impostare e mantenere i testbed del software di volo flat-sat

• Eseguire studi commerciali relativi al software che coprono capacità di elaborazione, memoria, tempismo, larghezza di banda, autonomia, affidabilità e tolleranza di guasto.

• Sviluppare in tempo reale, eventi-driven, autonomi, sincronizzazione e funzioni software relative a GNC, dove necessario.

• Stabilire e mantenere basi software, il controllo di configurazione, la versione, costruire l'automazione, l'integrazione continua, la gestione del rilascio e requisiti di tracciabilità.

• Sviluppare ed eseguire test unità software di volo, condurre l'integrazione, software-in-the-loop, processore-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop, e le attività di verifica e validazione a livello di sistema.

• Supporta la gestione del rischio del software, l'indagine di anomalia, la gestione non conformità e le schede di revisione tecnica.

• Supporta l'assemblaggio, l'integrazione e le attività di test, la messa in servizio, gli aggiornamenti software in volo, l'analisi della telemetria e le operazioni di missione.

• Contribuisci alle recensioni tecniche, ai concetti di missione, alle proposte e agli studi di fattibilità del software.

• Fornire assistenza tecnica a giovani ingegneri, ricercatori e team di studenti.

Profilo

Hai uno sfondo forte nello sviluppo di software incorporato e in tempo reale

Flight Software Systems Engineer für Weltraummissionen

80%-100%, Zürich, befristet

Druck
Druckerzeugnisse

Unter der Leitung von Prof. Dr. Thomas Zurbuchen bringt die ETH Zürich | Space weltraumbezogene Forschung, Bildung und Technologieentwicklung in der gesamten ETH Zürich zusammen. In Zusammenarbeit mit akademischen, industriellen und institutionellen Partnern entwickelt die Initiative neue Weltraummissionen, Instrumente und Technologien.

Diese Position wird als befristete Ernennung für eine erste Periode von zwei Jahren mit der Möglichkeit der Verlängerung angeboten.

Projekthintergrund

Ziel dieser Initiative ist es, einen zentralen Pool an Raumfahrt-Expertise innerhalb der ETH Zürich | Space zu etablieren und auszubauen. Dieser Pool unterstützt von der ETH Zürich geleitete Raumfahrtprojekte und Technologieprogramme und stärkt die Rolle der ETH Zürich im schweizerischen und internationalen Weltraumökosystem.

Der Flight Software Systems Engineer wird ein vielfältiges Portfolio von kleinen Raumfahrzeugen, wissenschaftlichen Instrumenten, Robotersystemen und Technologiedemonstratoren unterstützen. Die Arbeit umfasst ressourcenbeschränkte Missionen, die Integration mit extern gelieferten Raumfahrzeugplattformen, autonome Funktionen und zukünftige verteilte oder koordinierte Raumfahrzeugkonzepte. Diese Rolle knüpft an Systemtechnik, Avionik, Nutzlasten und Softwareentwicklung an und koordiniert sich mit externen Plattformanbietern und Mission Operations Teams.

Stellenbeschreibung

Als Teil des spezialisierten Ressourcenpools stellen Sie Flugsoftware und Softwaresystemtechnik-Know-how für mehrere Raumfahrtprojekte der ETH Zürich zur Verfügung. Sie werden von frühen Mission Formulierung und Software-Architektur durch Implementierung, Integration, Verifizierung, Startvorbereitung und Operationen beitragen.

Als Teil Ihrer Rolle werden Sie:

• Übernehmen Sie das technische Eigentum an zugewiesenen Flugsoftwareentwicklungen und fungieren Sie als primäre Softwareschnittstelle für Systemtechnik, Avionik, Nutzlastteams, Mission Operations und externe Plattformanbieter.

• Übersetzen Sie das Missionskonzept von Operationen in das Verhalten von Raumfahrzeugen und definieren Sie Flugsoftwarearchitekturen und funktionale Zerlegungen

• Weisen Sie Hardware-Software-Funktionen zu und definieren Sie die zugehörigen Softwareanforderungen und Schnittstellen.

• Übersetzen Sie Missions- und Systemanforderungen in Softwarespezifikationen, Schnittstellenkontrolldokumente, Betriebskonzepte und Verifizierungspläne.

• Entwicklung eingebetteter Flugsoftware in C und C++ und unterstützender Tools und Testskripte (z. B. Python), einschließlich Gerätetreiber, Telemetrie- und Telekommandohandling, Onboard-Datenmanagement, Anwendungssoftware und Fehlermanagementfunktionen.

• Integrieren Sie Flugsoftware mit Bordcomputern, Sensoren, Aktoren, Nutzlastelektronik, Kommunikationsschnittstellen, Bodensystemen und extern versorgten Raumfahrzeugplattformen.

• Einrichtung und Wartung von Testbeds für Flat-Sat-Flugsoftware

• Führen Sie softwarebezogene Handelsstudien durch, die Verarbeitungskapazität, Speicher, Timing, Bandbreite, Autonomie, Zuverlässigkeit und Fehlertoleranz abdecken.

• Entwickeln Sie bei Bedarf Echtzeit-, ereignisgesteuerte, autonome, Synchronisations- und GNC-bezogene Softwarefunktionen.

• Aufbau und Pflege von Software-Baselines, Konfigurationskontrolle, Versionierung, Build-Automatisierung, Continuous Integration, Release-Management und Anforderungsrückverfolgbarkeit.

• Entwicklung und Durchführung von Tests von Flugsoftwareeinheiten, Durchführung von Integrations-, Software-in-the-Loop-, Prozessor-in-the-Loop-, Hardware-in-the-Loop- und Validierungsaktivitäten auf Systemebene.

• Unterstützung von Software-Risikomanagement, Anomalieuntersuchungen, Non-Conformance-Handling und technischen Review Boards.

• Unterstützen Sie die Montage von Raumfahrzeugen und Nutzlasten, die Integration und Testaktivitäten, die Inbetriebnahme, Softwareupdates während des Fluges, die Telemetrieanalyse und den Missionsbetrieb.

• Tragen Sie zu technischen Überprüfungen, frühen Missionskonzepten, Vorschlägen und Machbarkeitsstudien für Software bei.

• Bieten Sie technische Unterstützung für Nachwuchsingenieure, Forscher und Studententeams.

Profil

Sie haben einen starken Hintergrund in eingebetteten und Echtzeit-Software-Entwicklung
descriptionByLocale.fr:
Ingénieur des systèmes de vol pour les missions spatiales

80%-100%, Zurich, durée déterminée

imprimer
Drucken

Dirigé par le Prof. Dr. Thomas Zurbuchen, ETH Zurich L'espace réunit la recherche, l'éducation et le développement technologique liés à l'espace dans l'ensemble de l'ETH Zurich. En collaboration avec des partenaires universitaires, industriels et institutionnels, l'initiative développe de nouvelles missions spatiales, des instruments et des technologies.

Ce poste est offert à titre d'engagement de durée déterminée pour une période initiale de deux ans, avec possibilité de prolongation.

Contexte du projet

L'objectif de cette initiative est d'établir et de développer un bassin centralisé d'expertise en ingénierie spatiale au sein de l'ETH Zurich. Cette piscine soutient les projets spatiaux et les programmes technologiques menés par l'ETH Zurich, renforçant ainsi le rôle de l'ETH Zurich dans l'écosystème spatial suisse et international.

L'ingénieur en systèmes logiciels de vol soutiendra un portefeuille diversifié de petits engins spatiaux, d'instruments scientifiques, de systèmes robotiques et de démonstrateurs technologiques. Le travail comprend des missions limitées en ressources, l'intégration avec des plates-formes spatiales fournies à l'extérieur, des fonctions autonomes et des concepts futurs distribués ou coordonnés. Ce rôle s'interface avec l'ingénierie des systèmes, l'avionique, les charges utiles et le développement de logiciels, et coordonne avec les fournisseurs externes de plateformes et les équipes opérationnelles de la mission.

Description du poste

Dans le cadre du pool de ressources spécialisé, vous fournirez une expertise en ingénierie de logiciels de vol et de systèmes logiciels sur plusieurs projets spatiaux de Zurich ETH. Vous contribuerez à la formulation de la mission et à l'architecture des logiciels par la mise en œuvre, l'intégration, la vérification, la préparation du lancement et les opérations.

Dans le cadre de votre rôle, vous:

• S'approprier techniquement les développements de logiciels de vol assignés et agir comme interface logicielle principale pour l'ingénierie des systèmes, l'avionique, les équipes de charge utile, les opérations de la mission et les fournisseurs de plateformes externes.

• Traduire le concept d'opérations de mission en comportements spatiaux et définir les architectures de logiciels de vol et les décompositions fonctionnelles

• Attribuer des fonctions matérielles et logicielles et définir les exigences et les interfaces des logiciels connexes.

• Traduire les exigences de la mission et du système en spécifications logicielles, documents de contrôle d'interface, concepts opérationnels et plans de vérification.

• Développer des logiciels de vol embarqués en C et C++ et des outils de support et des scripts de test (p. ex. Python), y compris les pilotes de périphériques, la télémétrie et le traitement des commandes, la gestion des données à bord, les logiciels d'application et les fonctions de gestion des erreurs.

• Intégrer les logiciels de vol avec les ordinateurs embarqués, les capteurs, les actionneurs, l'électronique de charge utile, les interfaces de communication, les systèmes au sol et les plates-formes spatiales fournies par l'extérieur.

• Mettre en place et entretenir des bancs d'essai de logiciels de vol à plat

• Effectuer des études commerciales liées au logiciel portant sur la capacité de traitement, la mémoire, le timing, la bande passante, l'autonomie, la fiabilité et la tolérance aux défauts.

• Développer des fonctions logicielles en temps réel, axées sur les événements, autonomes, de synchronisation et liées au GNC, au besoin.

• Établir et maintenir des bases de données logicielles, le contrôle de configuration, la version, l'automatisation de construction, l'intégration continue, la gestion des rejets et la traçabilité des exigences.

• Élaborer et exécuter des tests d'unités de logiciels de vol, effectuer des activités d'intégration, de logiciel dans la boucle, de processeur dans la boucle, de matériel dans la boucle et de vérification et de validation au niveau du système.

• Soutenir la gestion des risques liés aux logiciels, les enquêtes sur les anomalies, la gestion des non-conformités et les comités d'examen technique.

• Soutenir l'assemblage des engins spatiaux et des charges utiles, l'intégration et les activités d'essai, la mise en service, les mises à jour des logiciels en vol, l'analyse de télémétrie et les opérations de mission.

• Contribuer aux examens techniques, aux concepts de mission en début de mission, aux propositions et aux études de faisabilité des logiciels.

• Fournir des conseils techniques aux ingénieurs subalternes, aux chercheurs et aux équipes étudiantes.

Profil

Vous avez une solide expérience dans le développement de logiciels embarqués et en temps réel

jobs.description:
PhD Researcher

100%, Singapore, fixed-term

Drucken

The Singapore-ETH Centre was established in 2010 by ETH Zurich - The Swiss Federal Institute of Technology and Singapore’s National Research Foundation (NRF), as part of the NRF’s CREATE campus. As ETH Zurich's only research centre outside of Switzerland, the centre has strengthened the research capacity of ETH Zurich to develop sustainable solutions to global challenges in Switzerland, Singapore and the surrounding regions.

Set in Asia, in a rapidly urbanising region, the Singapore-ETH Centre aims to provide practical solutions to some of the most pressing challenges on urban sustainability, resilience and health through its programmes: Future Cities Lab Global (FCL Global) and Future Health Technologies (FHT) .

The centre serves as an intellectual hub for research, bringing together principal investigators and researchers from diverse disciplines and backgrounds. To promote the exchange of ideas and expertise, our researchers actively collaborate with universities and research institutes and engage with industry and government agencies to translate knowledge to practical solutions to real-world problems.

Project background

Fracture risk assessment today relies mainly on areal bone mineral density (DXA) which has limited discriminative power and lose accuracy over longer follow-up periods. Hip fractures carry the highest socioeconomic burden among osteoporotic fractures, yet they remain assessed largely from bone fragility alone, without properly accounting for fall biomechanics.

Our group's simulation-based models capture how bone strength and fall mechanics combine to determine an individual's hip fracture risk, offering a more personalised picture than bone density alone. However, these simulations are computationally expensive, making them clinically impractical at scale. The solution lies in image-based, data-driven (AI) models that learn to predict personalised fracture risk directly from routine bone-density or CT scans in seconds.

This PhD project will build and validate such AI models, extending them from single-timepoint prediction to longitudinal, personalised fracture-risk trajectories using repeat imaging. The successful candidate will therefore be working primarily as an AI/image-processing researcher, developing deep-learning models for medical images.

Job description

The PhD candidate will be embedded into a team of researchers developing AI models that produce markers of musculoskeletal health directly from medical images, as part of the Future Health Technologies 2 (FHT2) programme.

Some key components in the work are:

• Developing AI/deep-learning models, including generative and image-assessment approaches, that predict an individual's fracture risk directly from bone-density and CT images.

• Extending these image-based models to longitudinal data, to forecast personalised bone-ageing trajectories and future fracture risk from repeat scans and clinical risk factors.

• Validating model predictions against biomechanical simulations and real-world fracture outcomes across cohorts.

• Co-supervision of MSc and BSc students.

Please note that the employment will be at the Singapore-ETH Centre in Singapore, and local working regulations will apply.

Profile

Applicants are invited to apply for a PhD position at the Singapore-ETH Centre (SEC) in Singapore, available from 1 Dec 2026 (flexible start date). Funding is provided for up to four years.

• Applicants should hold an MSc degree and have a strong background in computer science, engineering, mathematics, physics, or a related quantitative discipline. After successful completion of studies, the PhD degree will be awarded by ETH Zurich.

• Candidates should be capable of working largely independently on complex research topics and demonstrate strong motivation.

• We are particularly interested in applicants with a strong foundation in machine learning/deep learning and medical image

Hip fractures carry the highest socioeconomic burden among osteoporotic fractures, yet they remain assessed largely from bone fragility alone, without properly accounting for fall biomechanics.

Our group's simulation-based models capture how bone strength and fall mechanics combine to determine an individual's hip fracture risk, offering a more personalised picture than bone density alone. However, these simulations are computationally expensive, making them clinically impractical at scale. The solution lies in image-based, data-driven (AI) models that learn to predict personalised fracture risk directly from routine bone-density or CT scans in seconds.

This PhD project will build and validate such AI models, extending them from single-timepoint prediction to longitudinal, personalised fracture-risk trajectories using repeat imaging. The successful candidate will therefore be working primarily as an AI/image-processing researcher, developing deep-learning models for medical images.

Job description

The PhD candidate will be embedded into a team of researchers developing AI models that produce markers of musculoskeletal health directly from medical images, as part of the Future Health Technologies 2 (FHT2) programme.

Some key components in the work are:

• Developing AI/deep-learning models, including generative and image-assessment approaches, that predict an individual's fracture risk directly from bone-density and CT images.

• Extending these image-based models to longitudinal data, to forecast personalised bone-ageing trajectories and future fracture risk from repeat scans and clinical risk factors.

• Validating model predictions against biomechanical simulations and real-world fracture outcomes across cohorts.

• Co-supervision of MSc and BSc students.

Please note that the employment will be at the Singapore-ETH Centre in Singapore, and local working regulations will apply.

Profile

Applicants are invited to apply for a PhD position at the Singapore-ETH Centre (SEC) in Singapore, available from 1 Dec 2026 (flexible start date). Funding is provided for up to four years.

• Applicants should hold an MSc degree and have a strong background in computer science, engineering, mathematics, physics, or a related quantitative discipline. After successful completion of studies, the PhD degree will be awarded by ETH Zurich.

• Candidates should be capable of working largely independently on complex research topics and demonstrate strong motivation.

• We are particularly interested in applicants with a strong foundation in machine learning/deep learning and medical image
